497.skill_description: Patiently and non-judgmentally listen to their inner thoughts and experiences, respond with genuine empathy and positive attention, allow full expression and emotional release, alleviate tension and loneliness, and lay the foundation of a safe and trusting alliance.
497.when_to_use: The information collection and assessment stage of the first session, and the early crisis stage when the client needs to be understood and contained.
497.trigger: Continuously recounting exam-preparation experiences, interpersonal troubles, or symptoms; Low mood, sobbing, tense unease, needing to be understood and supported.

176.skill_description: Respond to the client's narratives and emotions such as sadness, anger, and grievance with sincere understanding and unconditional positive attention, reducing the sense of being negated and creating a safe atmosphere, encouraging willingness to engage and building the Work alliance.
176.when_to_use: At the beginning of the Evaluative session, or when talking about dormitory and family troubles.
176.trigger: Low, sad, speaking softly, avoiding eye contact or shedding tears; expressing negative emotions such as grievance, anger, and self-blame.

139.skill_description: Maintain focused, non-judgmental Listening, with minimal encouragement and pauses, allowing them to pour out and vent freely until emotions stabilize, then advancing assessment and handling, enhancing the sense of being understood and mutual trust.
139.when_to_use: Early in the session and at the emotional expression stage, or when a strong emotional response occurs in any session.
139.trigger: Actively expressing Loneliness, gloom, inferiority, Anxiety; crying loudly, continuously narrating grievances, finding it hard to control themselves.

142.skill_name: Promptly affirm and encourage effort and progress
142.skill_description: When the client adopts self-regulation or shows positive changes, give timely specific affirmation and praise, conveying respect and support, reinforcing self-efficacy and motivation to change, and consolidating the counseling relationship and cooperation.
142.when_to_use: When positive behaviors or Emotion management progress appear in the first few sessions, homework feedback, or after practice.
142.trigger: Avoiding arguments, using venting, taking medication on time, completing exercises, or reporting concrete improvements such as reduced Anxiety and better sleep.

480.skill_description: Timely identify and use emotional response statements to mark and validate the client's hardship and difficulty, responding directly with understanding and acceptance, moderately normalizing the stress experience, enhancing the sense of being seen and understood, and stabilizing the counseling relationship.
480.when_to_use: Used when key emotional nodes appear in the first stage and afterward, or when talking about emotional fluctuation caused by comparison, self-blame, and pressure.
480.trigger: Choking up, tearing, changes in speech rate, tense posture; speech containing 'Anxiety, disappointment, failure, I cannot do it, useless', etc.

501.skill_name: Building connection with Listening, Empathy, and respect
501.skill_description: In the first or early sessions, receive their confused narration with patient listening, emotional empathy, and a respectful attitude, respond to emotions, quickly create an alliance of being understood and safe, and promote subsequent cooperation and information acquisition.
501.when_to_use: At the first consultation or early relationship-building stage, when trust needs to be quickly gained and an alliance formed.
501.trigger: Head down, furrowed brows, Low mood; actively recounting confusion and chaos, tense Anxiety.

527.skill_name: Explain the method's rationale and introduce relaxation training
527.skill_description: Before early technical intervention, introduce the principles of the rational emotive therapy ABC and such, and arrange or demonstrate relaxation training, letting the client experience the difference between tension and relaxation, promoting understanding, identification, and cooperation with the method.
527.when_to_use: At the start of the second session or before early technical intervention.
527.trigger: When Anxiety is significant and sleep is poor; when doubting the method's effectiveness and rationale or needing to enhance cooperation.

529.skill_name: Guiding breathing relaxation to calm emotions
529.skill_description: Guide slow, regular breathing relaxation to reduce physiological arousal and emotional agitation, contain high-intensity emotions, and create a controllable and stable state and atmosphere for subsequent communication and discussion of the problem.
529.when_to_use: At the beginning of the session or during narration, when emotions run high and affect expression and communication.
529.trigger: Continuous crying, agitated unease, rapid breathing, chest tightness, or somatic tension difficult to verbalize.

144.skill_name: Timely affirmation and praise consolidating change
144.skill_description: For feasible strategies and new attempts proposed by the client, give concrete affirmation and praise promptly and naturally, and when summarizing progress name their strengths and changes, raising confidence and security and consolidating the positive connection and change motivation.
144.when_to_use: After discussing alternative behaviors or situational plans, when trying new actions, and at the closing stage when summarizing progress.
144.trigger: When proposing action plans such as calming down and negotiating with classmates first; demonstrating skills or completing homework and feeding back changes and improvements.

160.skill_name: Open-ended Questioning guiding narrative and Collecting data
160.skill_description: Use open-ended questions to invite the client to describe their developmental history, current situation, and distress in detail, encouraging free expression, obtaining key information and enhancing the experience of being Listened to, balancing data collection with relationship building.
160.when_to_use: The information collection part of the diagnostic assessment and relationship-building stage, when the client needs to be guided to unfold their narrative.
160.trigger: When the narrative is scattered or too brief, not knowing where to start; needing a more comprehensive description of experiences and problems and they are willing to cooperate.

297.skill_description: Use open-ended questions focused on feelings to guide the client to express current experiences (such as 'What feelings do you have?'), let the emotions be seen and accepted, start empathy and connection, and promote deeper exploration and understanding.
297.when_to_use: Used when presenting a genogram or discussing key events, or when emotional expression is sparse and the emotional level needs to be entered to deepen the relationship and understanding.
297.trigger: When there are general statements, insufficient details, or emotional cues such as pauses, choking, or tears.

482.skill_name: Identifying A and C and linking A→B→C
482.skill_description: Through Questioning and emotional reflection, guide the client to first concretize the emotional/behavioral consequences (C) and the trigger event (A), then notice and analyze the irrational beliefs (B) within; restate in the client's own words 'when A happens, you believe B, therefore C appears', emphasizing that C is caused by B rather than directly by A, clearly depicting the chain and the maintenance cycle, laying the foundation for conceptualization and subsequent Intervention.
482.when_to_use: In the ABC analysis of the first-stage session and each subsequent homework review, or when the narrative is vague and the distress mechanism needs to be quickly clarified and the change direction focused.
482.trigger: When the client narrates irritability, ambivalence, or submits specific event records; reports consequences such as depression, Anxiety, avoidance, and tends to attribute emotions directly to the event itself.

208.skill_name: Explain ABC and build a shared framework
208.skill_description: Explain to the client the emotion ABC model, explain the connections of situation (A), belief (B), emotion/behavior consequence (C), clarify that 'C is not directly caused by A but is determined by B', and with their current difficulty demonstrate the usage of the chain, helping them accept this model as a basis for analysis and subsequent intervention.
208.when_to_use: After establishing a preliminary relationship, in the psychoeducation/conceptualization starting step of entering the cognitive behavioral stage; before entering rational emotive therapy or needing to unify the counseling language.
208.trigger: The client attributes emotions entirely to the event itself, feels confused about 'why it is like this', or is unfamiliar with the ABC model and understands it vaguely.

194.skill_name: Identifying and naming the irrational belief B
194.skill_description: On the basis of clarified A and C, capture and record verbatim absolutist Automatic thoughts such as 'must/should/always/all/nobody', overgeneralization, catastrophizing, etc., label them as B and categorize them into typical types, distinguish facts from evaluations, as targets for disputation and restructuring.
194.when_to_use: A and C are already fairly clear but the distress persists, when it is necessary to focus on the belief level for cognitive processing and restructuring; or after clarifying A, asking 'what thought flashed through your mind at that time'.
194.trigger: When extreme language and self-deprecating statements appear, such as 'must surpass others', 'will definitely fail', 'nobody likes me', etc.; repeatedly interpreting others' behavior in absolutist language.

157.skill_name: Debating and generating rational alternative beliefs
157.skill_description: For identified irrational beliefs, use the method of disputing beliefs, examining them from three aspects — evidence, logic, and utility — providing more reasonable alternative interpretations and generating alternative beliefs, reinforcing them in the session to reduce consequences like Anxiety/depression and guide subsequent actions.
157.when_to_use: After completing ABC chain identification and confirming the presence of irrational beliefs, entering the cognitive restructuring and working-through stage.
157.trigger: The client insists on extremist, catastrophizing, or must-type beliefs (such as 'they will definitely take revenge on me' and 'everything is finished') and emotions/functioning are impaired.

251.skill_name: Map the A-B-C chain within the situation
251.skill_description: Around recent key situations, concretize the time, place, and others' reactions, capture current Automatic thoughts/beliefs, mark the corresponding emotional intensity and behavioral responses, forming a clear situation-thought-emotion/behavior chain, providing a basis for identifying irrational cognitions and formulating Intervention.
251.when_to_use: During the case conceptualization stage or when reviewing a recent high-emotion event, the narrative needs to be structured into A-B-C for analysis and focus.
251.trigger: When describing multiple typical distressing events accompanied by strong emotional fluctuations or functional impairment (such as insomnia, avoidance), or quickly making negative inferences about interpersonal/Learning situations.

425.skill_name: Label and connect the emotional/behavioral consequence C
425.skill_description: Guide the client to identify and quantify their emotional and behavioral responses at the time (such as Anxiety, helplessness, avoidance, impulsivity, etc.), emphasizing their correspondence with belief B, completing the A-B-C chain and marking the maintenance mechanism, providing a baseline for goal setting and Intervention evaluation.
425.when_to_use: During assessment feedback and cognitive discussion, or after identifying B, to complete C and Clarify the problem mechanism.
425.trigger: When reporting strong negative emotions, somatic activation, or behavioral changes such as avoidance/Withdrawal, and tending to attribute suffering to the event itself.

301.skill_name: Integrate situations and beliefs to draw the A-B-C
301.skill_description: Jointly analyze key situations and irrational beliefs with the client, systematically extracting A, B, and the corresponding emotional/behavioral C, clarifying the 'event-belief-consequence' relationship and comparing evidence, forming an ABC-chain understanding of the case, stimulating motivation to change, and orienting subsequent Intervention.
301.when_to_use: The core scenes and beliefs have been collected, and they need to be integrated into an A-B-C chain and enter the case conceptualization period.
301.trigger: The client mentions both a specific event and marked emotional distress, or negatively predicts others' attitudes and avoids out of worry.

305.skill_name: Examining evidence and generating alternative thoughts
305.skill_description: After identifying negative Automatic thoughts, discuss supporting and refuting evidence, distinguish facts from inferences, transform the single negative interpretation into more balanced, reality-based alternative thinking, and observe how emotions improve with the alternative beliefs.
305.when_to_use: After completing the sorting of A and B, entering the cognitive restructuring stage, to question irrational beliefs and form alternative thinking.
305.trigger: Insists on beliefs such as mind reading / catastrophizing (such as 'I will be laughed at'), emotions / behavior worsen accordingly and she can describe the associated reactions.

326.skill_name: Explain ABC and correct faulty attributions
326.skill_description: Use plain language to explain the relationship among A (event), B (belief), and C (emotion/behavior), clarifying that 'C is not directly caused by A but determined by B', aligning the framework with case materials, to establish a common language and pave the way for subsequent identification and correction of beliefs.
326.when_to_use: In the psychoeducation and conceptualization part of the initial assessment / early sessions, or before entering rational emotive therapy intervention.
326.trigger: When the client attributes maladaptive emotions entirely to events, has a vague understanding of the mechanism, or is unfamiliar with the ABC model.

256.skill_name: Capture and record automatic thoughts (B) verbatim
256.skill_description: After clarifying the trigger situation A, ask 'what was going through your mind at the time', recording Automatic thoughts and negative assumptions item by item in the client's own words, distinguishing evaluations from facts, forming a B list, to target subsequent evidence testing and cognitive restructuring.
256.when_to_use: After clarifying the situation, entering the stage of identifying cognitive components, to sort out the transition from A to B.
256.trigger: When absolutist, self-blaming, or self-deprecating statements appear (such as 'I am too stupid', 'they are excluding me'), but the thoughts are not yet externalized.

235.skill_name: Concretizing and defining the trigger situation A
235.skill_description: Through concretizing Questioning, guide the client back to a clear, observable trigger situation, clarifying time, place, people, and key details, locking in the starting point of A, providing a framework for subsequently extracting Automatic thoughts and emotions/behaviors.
235.when_to_use: At the beginning of cross-sectional analysis in the assessment and conceptualization stage or identifying Automatic thoughts, when needing to build the A-B-C chain.
235.trigger: Vaguely expresses 'very uncomfortable / always low' without concrete event clues, or events and emotions are entangled and hard to focus.

487.skill_name: Defining and pairing the activating event A
487.skill_description: Around the client's recent narratives, define the specific inducing event A (such as failing to be selected, conflicts), restore key fragments along the timeline, and pair them with the corresponding C, anchoring the starting point of this analysis, providing a basis for identifying B and subsequent disputation.
487.when_to_use: In the diagnostic assessment and counseling-relationship building stage or the early phase of psychological help, when the starting point of the ABC chain needs to be established.
487.trigger: When repeatedly mentioning specific events like 'not meeting Anticipation' or 'arguing with roommates', with scattered narratives or not yet distinguishing events from evaluations.

182.skill_name: Quantify beliefs and emotions and re-evaluate before and after
182.skill_description: Have the client quantify the degree of belief in key automatic thoughts and the intensity of related emotions (e.g., 0-10 points / percentages); after cognitive testing or replacement, rate again and compare the before-and-after changes to examine the effect of cognitive adjustment on C.
182.when_to_use: After identifying B, entering the testing and restructuring stage; or after completing one cognitive restructuring, entering consolidation/summary feedback.
182.trigger: When deeply convinced of negative beliefs without doubt, or needing to monitor Intervention effects; having proposed new, more reasonable ideas and ready to assess emotional changes.

203.skill_description: After clarifying A and B, systematically sort out and quantify the corresponding emotional, somatic, and behavioral consequences (such as Anxiety, insomnia, Withdrawal, difficulty concentrating, etc.), recording frequency and impact, clarifying the scope and severity of C, providing a basis for goal setting and Intervention evaluation.
203.when_to_use: After clarifying the trigger event, completing the consequence link in the ABC chain; after identifying B, summarizing C simultaneously or subsequently.
203.trigger: When reporting functional impairment signals such as Anxiety, depression, Avoids communication, Learning Decreased efficiency, and sleep problems.

284.skill_name: Dispute B and develop counter/alternative thinking
284.skill_description: Record irrational beliefs item by item, initiate disputation through factual, logical, and utility Questioning, use reverse thinking such as 'are there other possibilities / good exceptions' to generate reasonable alternative beliefs, comparing emotional/behavioral changes before and after to consolidate the correction.
284.when_to_use: During and after disputing B, to consolidate correction and form alternative views, reducing consequences like Anxiety/depression.
284.trigger: Difficulty spontaneously proposing alternative views, clinging to thinking patterns such as 'must/definitely/utterly awful'.

135.skill_name: Quantifying emotional intensity and setting goals
135.skill_description: Guide the client to quantify the intensity of the current emotional consequence (C) with 0-10 or percentages, record the initial value and target value, and re-measure subsequently, as a reference and adjustment basis for ABC analysis and intervention effects.
135.when_to_use: At initial assessment, mood checks in each session, or when comparing after key Interventions, to establish and track the baseline.
135.trigger: The client has difficulty clearly describing the degree of emotions, or hopes to objectify changes and goal attainment.

309.skill_name: Assign belief-comparison homework to consolidate rational beliefs
309.skill_description: Assign Homework comparing the originally listed irrational beliefs with the newly built rational beliefs item by item, reflecting on their different impacts on emotions/behaviors, promoting daily practice and review to consolidate rational evaluation and prevent relapse.
309.when_to_use: After the disputation and replacement phase is complete, entering the working-through and consolidation stage, serving as out-of-session practice and maintenance of effects.
309.trigger: The client has formed a preliminary rational belief and is willing to complete written exercises to consolidate and verify the effect.

336.skill_name: Socratic identification and testing of B
336.skill_description: Around specific events, use Socratic Questioning to clarify the trigger situation A and the ideas/beliefs B, coherently probing their evidence, conditions, and consequences, testing overgeneralization and absolutist conclusions, loosening beliefs and forming more reality-based cognitive evaluations.
336.when_to_use: When conducting ABC analysis and cognitive restructuring, needing Questioning to promote self-Reflection and correct irrational beliefs.
336.trigger: Fixated on rigid beliefs such as 'must / definitely' or drawing extreme conclusions from few clues, emotions / behavior amplified by them.

365.skill_name: Emphasize event neutrality and replace with rational beliefs
365.skill_description: Explain that emotions stem from evaluations of events rather than the events themselves, distinguishing rational from irrational beliefs; after disputation, guide replacing old beliefs with more realistic, tolerant cognitions (such as correcting from wholesale negation to more objective statements), rebuilding thinking with evidence and reducing Anxiety/depression.
365.when_to_use: After disputation, when the client acknowledges the contradiction and begins to loosen the old beliefs, used to consolidate the new rational cognition.
365.trigger: The client shows more balanced evidence or willingness to revise original views, showing cognitive flexibility.

287.skill_name: Socratic sorting and examining of the A-B-C
287.skill_description: Review key events with continuous questioning, asking in sequence 'what were you thinking at the time / how did you feel / what did you do afterward', stringing A-B-C together, and around the automatic thought search for supporting and disconfirming evidence, explore the worst consequence and its likelihood, reducing the persuasiveness of catastrophizing and labeling conclusions.
287.when_to_use: When discussing specific events with strong Automatic thoughts and heightened emotions, to identify and challenge irrational beliefs and generate alternative ideas.
287.trigger: When absolute/labeling statements like 'I am not worthy of being loved' or 'I am very incompetent' appear, accompanied by significant negative emotions or impulsive behaviors.

243.skill_name: Guiding and assigning the three-column form to record A-B-C
243.skill_description: Demonstrate and guide the use of a three-column table (situation — Automatic thoughts — emotion), recording immediately when negative emotions appear, correcting errors such as writing evaluations into the situation, training to condense Automatic thoughts into one sentence, and accordingly examining biases and generating more balanced alternative thinking.
243.when_to_use: During initial teaching or the B-identification training stage; as daily self-monitoring and out-of-session homework to consolidate ABC identification and reappraisal.
243.trigger: When the client's understanding of the emotion-cognition relationship is confused, the narrative is fragmented, or the client is willing to complete structured recording homework.

390.skill_name: Check past psychiatric visits, diagnoses, and medication history
390.skill_description: Ask about and record whether there is a history of mental illness, psychiatric visits/hospitalizations, past diagnoses and medication experiences (including drug names and efficacy), verify whether they have received counseling or treatment, clarifying negative or positive information, to assist current diagnosis, assess relapse risk, and formulate the counseling plan.
390.when_to_use: At the initial consultation or past-history collection stage, before formulating diagnosis and plan or starting systematic assessment.
390.trigger: At initial consultation, previous mental illness or medical history needs to be ruled out; the client mentions having visited a doctor/taken medication/received counseling, or file information is missing and needs supplementing.

413.skill_name: Ask about personal and family medical history
413.skill_description: Collect and record personal history of major physical illness and mental illness, family history of mental illness, noting positive or negative results (such as no major organic disease, no family mental illness), to rule out major problems, assess comorbidity and genetic risk, and support diagnosis and plan formulation.
413.when_to_use: Medical history inquiry in the initial assessment and diagnosis stage, or when severe mental illness and important comorbid factors need to be ruled out.
413.trigger: When needing to determine whether there is a family history of mental illness or personal past illness; when the client is unclear about their own or family medical history.

462.skill_name: Asking about hospital diagnoses and psychiatric visit/hospitalization history
462.skill_description: Systematically ask whether they have ever sought care at a hospital or psychiatric outpatient/inpatient service, record diagnosis, hospitalization, and medication experiences, and check physical examination conclusions, to assess past medical history and treatment response and assist current judgment and relapse risk assessment.
462.when_to_use: At the history-taking stage, for evaluating medical history and plan formulation, or when materials are missing and need supplementing.
462.trigger: When the client mentions or denies hospital diagnoses/psychiatric visits, or explains examination conclusions, not yet using psychiatric medication, and other such information.

463.skill_name: Verify past counseling or therapy experiences
463.skill_description: Ask whether they have received counseling or other psychotherapy, recording the number of sessions, timing, and effects, clarifying negative or positive information, understanding past Intervention responses and compliance, to provide reference for current counseling goals and plans.
463.when_to_use: Before collecting past history and formulating the counseling plan, or when first-visit medical history information is missing.
463.trigger: When the client reports having or having had counseling experiences, or indicates this is their first visit.

129.skill_name: Record psychiatric diagnoses and treatment history
129.skill_description: Record the first diagnosis, follow-up visits, diagnostic conclusions, and Therapeutic process (such as medication, hospitalization) as well as efficacy and compliance, forming a past treatment trajectory, to provide a basis for current diagnosis and Intervention plans.
129.when_to_use: During history taking and medical information verification, before formulating the plan.
129.trigger: When the client describes clues of hospital diagnosis, two months of treatment without improvement, re-diagnosis, and continued medication.

416.skill_name: Verify recent medical examinations and organic-exclusion results
416.skill_description: Collect multiple medical visit and examination experiences and conclusions, recording information such as 'no organic lesions found yet', to support the current diagnosis, referral decisions, and Intervention plan formulation.
416.when_to_use: When assessing prior medical history or needing to rule out the influence of physical illness.
416.trigger: When the client mentions having sought medical examinations multiple times or having worries about physical condition.

473.skill_name: Verify psychiatric diagnosis and current medication status
473.skill_description: Ask about and verify past and current psychiatric diagnoses, treatment institutions, and medication use, recording adherence to medical advice, follow-up arrangements, and attitude changes, to provide a basis for Intervention and referral plans.
473.when_to_use: At initial assessment or when the condition is more severe and collaboration with and referral to the medical side are needed.
473.trigger: When the client mentions psychiatric visits/medication or presents hospital diagnostic information, or shows resistance to continuing medication.

282.skill_name: Learn about past counseling experiences and outcomes
282.skill_description: Ask about the timing, frequency, and impact or changes of past counseling, assessing past Intervention responses and compliance, to provide reference for current counseling goals and plans.
282.when_to_use: Before formulating current counseling goals and plans, when assessing the effects of past Interventions.
282.trigger: When the client mentions having received psychological counseling or related cognitive and behavioral changes.

130.skill_name: Verifying past counseling and psychiatric treatment history
130.skill_description: Learn about past psychological counseling history, symptom history, and family history, verify whether psychological counseling and psychiatric medical visits/treatment have occurred, clarify whether this is the first help-seeking, providing a basis for relapse and risk assessment and plan formulation.
130.when_to_use: The information collection and assessment stage of the first session, or the prior-history collection segment.
130.trigger: When the counselor collects past counseling/treatment history; when the client is visiting for the first time or is uncertain about past medical history.

173.skill_name: Verifying personal medical conditions and family psychiatric history
173.skill_description: Ask about and record personal history of major physical illness and family history of mental illness, clarifying such as 'No major physical illness, no family mental illness', for diagnostic exclusion and risk assessment.
173.when_to_use: The stage of collecting past medical history and medical-seeking experiences.
173.trigger: When the client has not yet clarified past illness history or family psychiatric burden needs to be ruled out.

502.skill_name: Verify psychiatric diagnoses, hospitalizations, and psychotherapy experiences
502.skill_description: Recording the formal diagnosis, the start and end and duration of hospitalization, psychotherapy experience, and follow-up arrangements, forming an objective medical history framework to assist the current assessment and plan formulation.
502.when_to_use: During past medical history collection and when external medical record information needs to be integrated.
502.trigger: When the client mentions experiences of hospitalization/medical visits, being diagnosed, or having received psychological treatment.

424.skill_name: Asking about and recording family history of mental illness
424.skill_description: Collect information such as 'no family history of mental illness' as the basis for differential diagnosis and comorbidity risk assessment, helping rule out familial tendencies of related mental disorders.
424.when_to_use: During the diagnostic assessment and differential diagnosis data collection stage.
424.trigger: When family history needs to be understood or the client mentions family health status.

250.skill_name: Record psychiatric hospitalization and medication treatment history
250.skill_description: Records in detail emergency admissions, psychiatric hospitalizations, and the names of medications used and the treatment process, combined with treatment recommendations and effects, as the basis for the current diagnosis and plan formulation.
250.when_to_use: When reviewing past medical history and family history or during history taking.
250.trigger: When the client or medical record shows emergency visits, hospitalization, and current or past medication information.

511.skill_name: Verify crisis medical interventions and examination experiences
511.skill_description: Verify whether emergencies, hospitalizations, or other important medical interventions have occurred, recording time, causes, and outcomes/examination conclusions (such as no organic cause found yet), for current risk assessment and crisis plan formulation and updates.
511.when_to_use: During the medical history and risk assessment stage, to identify high-risk events and handling records or when medical exclusion is needed.
511.trigger: When the client mentions self-injury/suicidal ideation, medication overdose, or sudden crisis experiences, or has sought medical examination.

169.skill_name: Inquiring about and recording family psychiatric history
169.skill_description: Ask whether family members have had mental illness and record truthfully (such as 'no family history of mental illness'), to assess family risk and support systems, providing background information for diagnosis and Intervention.
169.when_to_use: When collecting past medical history and assessing risk.
169.trigger: When the client mentions family members or is asked about family medical history.

295.skill_name: Collect past counseling experiences and outcomes
295.skill_description: Record the number, timing, frequency, and subjective effects of past counseling or guidance, assessing past Intervention responses and compliance, to avoid repetition and optimize this counseling's strategies and technique selection.
295.when_to_use: When formulating this counseling's strategies or organizing the psychological problem history, assessing past Intervention responses.
295.trigger: When the client mentions having received psychological counseling, family/couples counseling, or completed psychological tests.

225.skill_name: Inventory past help-seeking and medical-seeking paths and their effects
225.skill_description: Systematically inventory experiences of seeking help from others and medical examinations and their effects, sorting out the help-seeking path and the effectiveness of previous Interventions, improving the treatment and support history, to provide reference for current assessment and plans.
225.when_to_use: The stage of collecting past medical history and help-seeking history, used to complete the diagnosis-treatment and support history.
225.trigger: When the client mentions having sought help from others or gone to the hospital for examination but the problem is not yet resolved or the effects are unclear.

190.skill_name: Integrate psychiatric visit diagnoses and medication information
190.skill_description: Ask whether they went to professional institutions for assessment, what diagnosis was received, and the current medication plan, recording follow-up arrangements and compliance, integrating medical information to coordinate on- and off-campus Interventions and formulate the counseling plan.
190.when_to_use: When the assessment stage requires integrating medical information or deciding on referral and collaboration.
190.trigger: When the client mentions being assessed, diagnosed with Anxiety and depression, or currently taking medication, or carries hospital diagnoses and medical advice.

159.skill_name: Sort out past and current medication history and efficacy
159.skill_description: Ask about and record medication names, dosages and duration, efficacy and adverse reactions (including reasons for discontinuation), experiences of refusing and resuming medication, and compliance, assessing how medication-related factors affect the current condition and treatment response.
159.when_to_use: When collecting prior medical history and diagnostic assessment, or formulating / collaborating on medication management.
159.trigger: When the client expresses concerns about medication efficacy/side effects, fluctuating compliance, or mentions experiences of stopping/resuming medication.

261.skill_name: Understanding current medication and compliance, and collaborating with the Doctor
261.skill_description: Understand the current drug treatment and compliance; with informed consent, collaborate with the psychiatrist to verify and coordinate, continuously monitoring the drug treatment and the need for coordination with counseling.
261.when_to_use: At the initial assessment and follow-up stages, when needing to integrate drug and psychological Interventions.
261.trigger: When there is psychiatric medication or compliance is unclear, or information requiring coordination with the Doctor is needed.

402.skill_name: Screen for psychotic symptoms and safety risks
402.skill_description: Confirm whether hallucinations, delusions, suicide tendencies, etc. appear, recording insight and intellectual status, to help rule out acute risks or major mental disorders, providing a basis for safety and referral decisions.
402.when_to_use: At the initial safety assessment and differential diagnosis stage, when risks need quick judgment.
402.trigger: When safety concerns arise, abnormal speech or behavior appears, or the history of psychotic symptoms needs confirmation.

175.skill_name: Asking about and recording details of medical visits and follow-ups after attempted suicide
175.skill_description: Ask in detail about the number, dates, methods of attempted suicides, emergency or hospitalization situations, and whether follow-ups were attended as advised, completing the medical and risk history records, to provide a basis for subsequent assessment and Intervention.
175.when_to_use: When assessing history of dangerous behavior and medical visits.
175.trigger: When the client reports past self-injury, suicide behaviors, or emergency and follow-up arrangements.

493.skill_name: Assessing self-injury/suicide history and current risk level
493.skill_description: Systematically ask about self-injury/suicide thoughts, plans, and past behaviors, clarifying current and past risk levels (e.g., has thoughts, no plan, no behavior), incorporating the information into risk assessment and providing a basis for crisis Intervention.
493.when_to_use: During initial safety-risk screening and follow-up monitoring.
493.trigger: When the client states they have self-injury or mentions despair, suicide-related content, or obvious self-injury marks are observed.

395.skill_description: Select typical events in the assessment narrative, gradually marking the trigger situation, current interpretations/Automatic thoughts, corresponding emotional intensity and behavioral responses, clarifying causal and cyclical relationships, forming a clear cross-sectional chain, to provide a basis for locating problems and subsequent Intervention.
395.when_to_use: After assessment and preliminary diagnosis, entering the conceptualization stage, or at the early conceptualization/review stage, when the operating mechanism of the current symptoms needs to be grasped.
395.trigger: When the client describes recent specific events accompanied by obvious Anxiety/low mood, physiological responses, or avoidant behaviors; when talking about Automatic thoughts clues but the links are unclear.

290.skill_name: Guiding thought records / change sheets to collect evidence and test thoughts
290.skill_description: Explain the thought-emotion relationship, guide the use of the Thought Record Sheet and thought-change record forms, recording situations, thoughts, and emotions, listing supporting and opposing evidence, identifying biases like mind reading and catastrophizing, observing emotional changes, and continuously improving the cross-sectional evidence base.
290.when_to_use: After being able to distinguish events, thoughts, and emotions, when inter-session monitoring and testing and correcting automatic thoughts on the horizontal chain are needed.
290.trigger: When negative thoughts are frequent, emotional intensity is high, or insomnia fluctuates; when obvious cognitive biases like mind reading and catastrophizing appear.

252.skill_name: Sort out core/intermediate beliefs and coping strategies
252.skill_description: Distill stable core beliefs, summarize 'if/should'-style Intermediate beliefs and rules, and identify compensatory and avoidant behavioral strategies, presenting the longitudinal structure from beliefs to coping patterns, as long-term Intervention targets.
252.when_to_use: After completing collection of early experiences and current-status information, before entering case conceptualization and formulating the problem list, or when the belief layer needs deepening after cross-sectional analysis.
252.trigger: When absolutist rules and self-blame/worthlessness themes repeatedly appear in speech; when behaviors show repeated avoidance, Withdrawal, or overcompensation.

269.skill_name: Connecting developmental experiences with the formation of core beliefs
269.skill_description: Review the growth history and important events, connect experiences such as high family expectations, beating and scolding, and lack of support with the current core/intermediate beliefs, elucidate the evolution of 'experience — forming beliefs — coping patterns', explain the deep sources, and point out the direction of long-term correction.
269.when_to_use: After identifying irrational beliefs, when needing to explore their origins and maintaining factors, completing the longitudinal conceptualization.
269.trigger: The client mentions experiences such as harsh discipline in childhood, being ostracized / humiliated, long-term lack of support, and current beliefs echo them.

191.skill_name: Using ABC/cross-sectional chains to sort out and name irrational thinking
191.skill_description: Around specific events, build A-B-C or cognition-emotion-behavior chains, identify and name irrational thinking such as black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and catastrophizing, clarifying their relationship with negative emotions and problem behaviors, to focus subsequent Intervention.
191.when_to_use: In the horizontal analysis stage of conceptualization or before entering cognitive restructuring, when the current mechanism needs to be clarified and the cognitive target locked in.
191.trigger: When extreme, catastrophizing, or denying expressions appear, accompanied by reactions such as Anxiety, depression, insomnia, and avoidance.

310.skill_name: Build an ABC chain to map current distress
310.skill_description: Jointly clarify the inducing event (A), immediate beliefs/interpretations (B), and emotional/behavioral consequences (C) with the client, externalizing them into a clear 'event-belief-response' chain, locating irrational beliefs and selecting Intervention points.
310.when_to_use: At the early stage of diagnosis and conceptualization (sessions 1-3), when needing to quickly clarify the current problem mechanism and Intervention targets.
310.trigger: When the client details events like breakups, not yet earning a degree, or being denied continued employment, accompanied by Anxiety, insomnia, and functional decline; when absolutist/catastrophizing statements appear.

209.skill_name: Integrates growth history and personality factors to carry out longitudinal conceptualization
209.skill_description: Sort out major life events and common coping, combining parenting styles and personality traits (such as introversion, external attribution, low sense of control), explaining the formation and maintenance of irrational beliefs and long-term patterns, laying the foundation for longitudinal conceptualization.
209.when_to_use: After the relationship is established and at the start of conceptualization, when the growth history and formative experiences need to be understood to distill deep beliefs and personality tendencies.
209.trigger: When the client is willing to narrate growing-up experiences or attributes distress to unchangeable external causes, expressing a lack of sense of control.

370.skill_name: Identifying Automatic thoughts in specific situations and linking them to emotions/behaviors
370.skill_description: Using recent interpersonal or Learning fragments as entry points, excerpting negative Automatic thoughts and clues, simultaneously marking trigger events, emotional intensity, and behavioral responses, establishing a situation-cognition-emotion/behavior linkage picture, enriching the cross-sectional conceptualization.
370.when_to_use: In the 1st-2nd assessments and subsequent early sessions, when needing to clarify trigger points and develop the cross-sectional conceptualization.
370.trigger: Situations such as dormitory conflict/feelings of exclusion and exam setbacks occur; thoughts such as 'They are targeting me' and 'I am so stupid', accompanied by panic, fear, or avoidance.

404.skill_name: Draw a cognitive conceptualization diagram integrating horizontal and vertical information
404.skill_description: Integrate situation - automatic thought - emotion/behavior with intermediate/core beliefs, growth experiences, and maintaining factors into a diagram or structured summary, forming a shared case conceptualization map, guiding goal setting and technique selection.
404.when_to_use: When cross-sectional and longitudinal information is fairly complete, to clearly present the problem mechanism and connect to Intervention planning and homework.
404.trigger: Typical situations, automatic thoughts, emotion ratings, core/intermediate beliefs, and growth history materials have been collected; structured presentation and alignment of key points are needed.

230.skill_name: Tracing early trauma and naming core belief themes
230.skill_description: Review experiences such as being left behind, scolded, bullied, and neglected, distilling core beliefs and intermediate rules like 'incapable/unlovable/no one is trustworthy', explaining how they are activated in the present and maintain distress, completing the longitudinal picture.
230.when_to_use: When current frustrations resonate with early experiences, and the source of the emotional intensity and reaction patterns needs to be explained.
230.trigger: When repeatedly mentioning early experiences such as being abandoned, lacking belonging, learned helplessness, or seeking attention through self-injury.

341.skill_name: Building and sharing the case conceptualization model to guide Intervention
341.skill_description: Diagrammatically connect the interaction of core beliefs, automatic thoughts, emotions / physiology, and safety / avoidance behaviors, forming a maintenance cycle model, and update it subsequently with feedback, used for goal and technique selection.
341.when_to_use: After completing cross-sectional and longitudinal information, summarizing the case and formulating the Intervention plan or updating it in stages.
341.trigger: Beliefs, situations, thoughts, emotions / physiology, and behavior information have been clarified and need systematic presentation to guide the next step.

499.skill_name: Explain and apply ABC analysis to current distress
499.skill_description: Explain the ABC theory to the client, using events around them as examples to distinguish A (event) / B (belief) / C (emotions and behavior), complete the self-problem explanation and draw the chain on the spot, establishing a common language and horizontal framework.
499.when_to_use: In the assessment and diagnosis stage and the early stage of counseling, used to establish a cross-sectional conceptualization and clarify the problem mechanism.
499.trigger: Attributes suffering entirely to external events, is confused about the source of emotions or asks about counseling approaches.

140.skill_name: Assign ABC self-monitoring and ranking homework
140.skill_description: Require recording the negative emotions / behaviors of the most recent stage and the corresponding A and B, and sort them by degree of distress; through structured written exercises, enhance self-awareness, form reviewable material, and support horizontal conceptualization.
140.when_to_use: After the client has understood the ABC framework, between two counseling sessions; after first data collection, when systematic sorting is needed.
140.trigger: The client has a preliminary awareness of their own distress but lacks systematic records; the counselor needs more concrete examples to support conceptualization.

200.skill_name: Summarizing repeated themes to distill core/intermediate beliefs
200.skill_description: On the basis of multiple situations and records, identify recurring self-evaluations and rules, summarizing them as Intermediate beliefs and more stable core beliefs, as key abstractions at the longitudinal level and Intervention targets.
200.when_to_use: After accumulating several horizontal cases, when it is necessary to rise to the belief level to explain widespread problems.
200.trigger: When stable thought themes repeatedly appear, such as 'if I refuse, others will be disappointed' or 'I cannot'.

381.skill_name: Identifying Intermediate beliefs and compensatory/avoidant strategies
381.skill_description: Record Intermediate beliefs in hypothesis/rule form, identifying compensatory or avoidant strategies developed to avoid confirming core beliefs (such as over-studying, rigid control, distancing), clarifying their functions and consequences, and locating the maintenance links.
381.when_to_use: In longitudinal conceptualization, when needing to connect core beliefs with daily behavior patterns to determine Intervention goals.
381.trigger: Rules such as 'must make everyone satisfied' and 'must work very hard' appear, accompanied by over-exertion or avoidance behavior.

496.skill_name: Identifying and classifying types of irrational beliefs
496.skill_description: In the B step, extract and name irrational beliefs, classifying them by type such as absolutizing, overgeneralization, and awfulizing, keeping the original words and marking the category, as clear targets for subsequent disputation and correction.
496.when_to_use: Used in the cognitive work stage after explaining REBT and sorting out the ABC, when key beliefs and error types need to be locked in.
496.trigger: Absolutist expressions such as 'definitely / should / everyone' appear, or self-evaluations and ideas that overgeneralize or catastrophize.

263.skill_name: Connects current patterns with growth experiences to distill core beliefs
263.skill_description: Taking the automatic thoughts and emotions / behaviors in typical situations as clues, trace back early caregiving and interpersonal experiences, compare the similarities and differences between past and present, and clarify the shaping path of historical experience on current beliefs and patterns.
263.when_to_use: After core beliefs initially emerge, used for longitudinal tracing and meaning integration.
263.trigger: Recalling early experiences triggers strong emotions or selective memory; clues such as parental expectations, being mocked/controlled are mentioned.

429.skill_name: Iteratively revise the conceptualization and plan based on assessment evidence
429.skill_description: According to the process evaluation and efficacy data, dynamically adjust the case conceptualization and the intervention path; when necessary, repeat the 'collect-organize-adjust' process or shift to new priority goals, ensuring the plan is consistent with the evidence of change.
429.when_to_use: When Intervention effects are poor, symptoms have not yet clearly improved, or new priority goals appear.
429.trigger: Signals such as blocked goal progress, limited scale improvement, or rebound in problem frequency.

291.skill_name: Translating conceptualization into staged goals and Intervention priorities
291.skill_description: On the basis of the case conceptualization, jointly confirm the main problems, distinguish short-term and long-term goals and sort them by impact and feasibility, match techniques and homework, and coordinate horizontal symptom management and longitudinal belief working-through.
291.when_to_use: After conceptualization is completed and shared, when entering the goal and plan formulation stage.
291.trigger: Key problems and causes are already clear, the client expresses willingness to change and needs to clarify stage goals and priorities.

328.skill_name: Feed back the conceptualization and provide ABC psychoeducation
328.skill_description: Feed back the assessment and conceptualization conclusions to the client, explain the core theory of ABC, clarify that emotions / behavior are mainly driven by beliefs rather than events themselves, and on this basis negotiate and determine the counseling goals and establish a common framework.
328.when_to_use: At the first consultation's result feedback and goal negotiation, or at the second session's opening homework feedback.
328.trigger: The client attributes the distress to the event itself; the event-belief-consequence relationship needs to be clarified to reach consensus.

254.skill_name: Integrate longitudinal information to map the vulnerability basis
254.skill_description: Based on developmental history and environmental clues (lack of recognition, major losses, and so on), summarize characteristics such as sensitive personality, low self-confidence, and tendency to internalize, connecting them to current self-blame and avoidance, as longitudinal susceptibility and maintenance factors.
254.when_to_use: Used when carrying out case conceptualization in the assessment or pre-group interview stage, when the history of the current problem and individual trait background need to be explained.
254.trigger: When narrating insufficient childhood care and emotional responsiveness, death of important loved ones, long-term neglect experiences, or introverted sensitivity, etc.

245.skill_name: Extract common automatic-thought patterns across situations
245.skill_description: In multiple three-column tables and cross-sectional records, comparing Automatic thoughts across different situations, summarizing common assumptions/rules, identifying stable maladaptive cognitive patterns, to provide focus for subsequent targeted Intervention.
245.when_to_use: After completing several three-column forms and event reviews, when it is necessary to integrate and distill horizontal patterns.
245.trigger: When similar interpretations and emotional responses repeatedly appear across different events, and the client finds it hard to see their commonality spontaneously.

244.skill_name: Using the three-column table to sort out situation-thought-emotion/behavior
244.skill_description: Use a three-column form to record typical situations, automatic thoughts and the corresponding emotions/behaviors, help distinguish thoughts from feelings, and classify and focus on the high-emotion entries, building clear material for horizontal chains.
244.when_to_use: In early counseling, entering information collection and case conceptualization, or at sessions 3-6 when entering cognitive processing.
244.trigger: When emotions are agitated — anger, Anxiety, or obvious maladaptive behaviors; when negative thoughts appear in the narrative.

280.skill_name: Disputing and testing irrational beliefs to promote correction
280.skill_description: Through Socratic Questioning and disputation, guiding the listing of evidence and counter-evidence, proposing alternative interpretations, challenging absolutist and catastrophizing irrational beliefs, fostering more reasonable expectations and beliefs, and improving emotions and behaviors.
280.when_to_use: After identifying key irrational beliefs, when cognitive restructuring and working-through are needed.
280.trigger: Insists on rigid views or a single hostile attribution, has difficulty correcting spontaneously, accompanied by marked negative emotions.

457.skill_name: Generate and itemize alternative beliefs to consolidate new views
457.skill_description: After the debate, itemize the rational alternative beliefs (such as 'everyone makes mistakes' and 'not everyone needs to approve'), make a comparison list and practice, so as to consolidate the conceptualization conclusions and guide subsequent intervention and action.
457.when_to_use: After completing the examination of the B belief, when it needs to be integrated into a clear conclusion and linked to treatment planning and homework.
457.trigger: Already able to answer dispute questions, shaken in the original belief and willing to accept alternative statements.

184.skill_name: Using the downward arrow to probe intermediate and core beliefs
184.skill_description: Taking a typical automatic thought as the starting point, continuously ask 'what does this mean / if that happens what then', probing down layer by layer to intermediate and core beliefs, and connect relevant early experiences and activating situations, completing the longitudinal conceptualization.
184.when_to_use: After identifying stable negative Automatic thoughts, when needing to explore deeper belief structures.
184.trigger: Automatic thoughts recur and are hard to change, or resonate markedly with early experiences, and global self-evaluations appear.

333.skill_name: Socratic Questioning to identify Automatic thoughts and link them to emotions/behaviors
333.skill_description: In specific trigger situations, use open, progressive Questioning to concretize and record Automatic thoughts, pointing out the ensuing emotional and behavioral responses, establishing a cross-sectional situation-cognition-emotion/behavior link.
333.when_to_use: Before entering cross-sectional analysis or cognitive restructuring, when key Automatic thoughts need to be found as Intervention targets.
333.trigger: When experiencing tension, tears, difficulty concentrating in social or academic situations, accompanied by thoughts like 'they are watching me' or 'I am very incompetent'.

444.skill_name: Socratic questioning to test beliefs and generate new perspectives
444.skill_description: Use evidence, logic, and functionality as the criterion, check facts and costs through Socratic questioning, compare rational and irrational beliefs, and promote perspective-taking and the formation of alternative rational beliefs and directions for action.
444.when_to_use: During the cognitive processing and consolidation period, to test rigid beliefs like 'not completing' or 'worthless' and promote alternatives.
444.trigger: Troubled by catastrophized or overgeneralized beliefs that are hard to loosen spontaneously, or stuck at the first step of decision-making.

266.skill_name: Verifying somatic history and examination results
266.skill_description: Ask whether there is major/chronic physical illness or disability, and verify past physical examination and hospital conclusions (such as 'no organic problems', 'examination results normal'), truthfully recording 'present/absent' and key details. Combining with current symptoms to judge the influence of medical factors, as the basis for differential diagnosis and whether medical referral is needed.
266.when_to_use: Before preliminary assessment and differential diagnosis, or when physiological factors and comorbidity need to be ruled out.
266.trigger: When the client reports somatic discomfort, physical problems, or past medical examinations; or when health information is missing and needs completion.

420.skill_name: Inquiring about and recording current physiological symptoms
420.skill_description: Around dizziness, fatigue, Decreased appetite, gastrointestinal discomfort, facial acne, trembling, memory decline, Sleep disorder, irregular menstruation, etc., ask item by item about frequency, duration, and degree of impact, recording 'no obvious physiological cause' when necessary, assessing the link with emotions/functioning and whether medical examination or coordinated Intervention is needed.
420.when_to_use: Used when assessing the impact of physical health on psychological problems and possible referral needs, or when assessing current illness state / symptom worsening.
420.trigger: When the client reports obvious somatic discomfort or physiological symptoms affecting daily functioning, or observable clues such as tiredness, weakness, or skin problems.

180.skill_name: Asking about sleep, diet, and somatic discomfort
180.skill_description: For changes like insomnia, easy awakening, and decreased food intake, further ask about chest tightness/pain, headache, shortness of breath, and other discomforts, as well as onset/end times, frequency, and severity, verifying past examination conclusions when necessary (such as no organic problems found yet), and combining appearance clues (haggard, thin) and physical performance (palpitations and panting during exercise) to assess impact.
180.when_to_use: The physical-health assessment at the initial visit and subsequent symptom tracking, or when medical conclusions need to be verified to judge their impact.
180.trigger: When the client mentions sleep/appetite changes or physical discomfort; when signs like weight loss or haggardness are observed; or when already examined but conclusions are unclear.

145.skill_name: Rule out physical illness and organic lesions
145.skill_description: Systematically ask about major physical illness, surgery, and chronic disease history, and verify key points of recent physical examinations/hospital checks, recording negative/positive conclusions (such as 'no abnormalities/no organic lesions'); supplementing family psychiatric history and overall health when necessary, ruling out medical factor interference, and supporting referral and Intervention decisions.
145.when_to_use: In the initial assessment and diagnostic exclusion stage, or when symptoms are physiologically related.
145.trigger: When medical comorbidity needs to be ruled out; when the client provides physical examination results or denies/is unclear about physical illness; when physiological anomaly clues like sleep or appetite issues exist.

412.skill_name: Assessing current physiological symptoms and nutrition
412.skill_description: Collect current conditions like insomnia, headache, lack of appetite, eating very little/occasionally not eating, weakness and fatigue, verifying symptoms such as stomach pain, menstrual pain, dizziness, and their frequency, and combining thin body type and others' observations, to judge the mutual influence with psychological symptoms and support/referral needs.
412.when_to_use: When assessing the physiological manifestations of the presenting complaint and judging support or referral; the initial stage of physical-health information collection.
412.trigger: When the client or others report marked changes in sleep, appetite, or physical strength; the client self-reports dizziness, fatigue, or worse sleep.

308.skill_name: Checking developmental posture and major medical history
308.skill_description: Ask about and record height, body shape and development, and history of major physical illness/disability, combining with recent physical examination conclusions to clarify whether organic lesions exist, forming a 'posture/development/medical history' overview (such as 'normal posture, good development, No major physical illness history/no organic lesions'), to rule out significant medical influence.
308.when_to_use: At the health inquiry part of the initial assessment to establish medical background, or when the influence of physical illness needs to be ruled out.
308.trigger: When the client has not yet actively provided health information, or when organic lesions need to be ruled out / a health baseline established.

323.skill_name: Recording somatic symptoms and sleep status
323.skill_description: Systematically record somatic presentations such as nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, palpitations, headache and dizziness, chest tightness, fatigue, and sleep/eating changes, clarifying frequency and severity, and paying attention to physiological signals like menstrual irregularity, linking to emotional and Learning function changes, indicating differential diagnosis and referral needs.
323.when_to_use: When assessing somatic symptoms related to mood disorders, or when history of present illness collection needs to grasp mind-body interaction.
323.trigger: When the client reports physiological signals such as diet and sleep problems, chest tightness, fatigue, or digestive discomfort.

456.skill_name: Verifying physical examination results to rule out organic causes
456.skill_description: Review or ask about physical examination/medical visit results, recording conclusions like 'no abnormalities found yet in physical examination/no organic lesions'; suggesting medical examination when necessary (such as fainting), and combining autonomic symptoms during episodes with general appearance, distinguishing somatic causes from psychological problems, to provide a basis for diagnosis and Intervention/referral.
456.when_to_use: In the assessment and diagnosis stage when medical factors need to be excluded, or when physical symptoms are pronounced or a major event has occurred.
456.trigger: When the client reports somatic discomfort such as tension, insomnia, or headache; has had physical examinations or worries about organic causes; or warning signs like fainting appear.

213.skill_name: Observing and recording appearance and physical-sign cues
213.skill_description: In the session record posture and visible physiological clues (such as a well-proportioned/thin build, pale complexion, dark eye circles, skin marks, intermittent scratching, stiff movements, nervously wringing hands), as an objective supplement on nutrition, sleep, and physical-mental state, assisting comprehensive judgment.
213.when_to_use: At the health and physical condition inquiry step and throughout the face-to-face assessment, objective observation records.
213.trigger: When visible posture/skin marks or tense behaviors are seen; when the client reports clues like sleep Anxiety that require ruling out obvious physiological abnormalities.

143.skill_name: Inquiring about sleep, appetite, and somatic reactions
143.skill_description: Detail insomnia (Difficulty falling asleep, early awakening, many dreams) and its duration, probing Decreased appetite and physical impact, and recording somatic responses like palpitations, headache, sweating, and pre-exam autonomic manifestations (sweaty palms, rapid heartbeat, nausea, frequent toilet visits), quantifying frequency and functional impact to determine relevance.
143.when_to_use: In the Evaluative session's health inquiry and symptom attribution stage, when physiological symptoms and changes need clarification.
143.trigger: When the client mentions clues like insomnia, many dreams, Decreased appetite, lack of physical strength, or palpitations.

515.skill_name: Observing and recording appearance and behavioral signs
515.skill_description: In the face-to-face consultation, record appearance and behavior clues such as body shape (on the thin side/slightly plump), dark circles, bloodshot eyes, pale face, changes in speech rate, speaking little with head lowered, scratch marks, nervously rubbing hands, and include the findings of the mental appearance examination (orientation, speech logic, posture and grooming), as objective evidence of the body-mind state.
515.when_to_use: The first-visit impression recording and face-to-face observation stage, and at the opening and throughout each session.
515.trigger: When on-site clues such as fatigue, skin damage, face-covering hairstyle, grooming tidiness, or psychomotor changes are visible.

459.skill_name: Recording height, weight, and physique indicators
459.skill_description: Record basic physical signs like height, weight, and body type in the general information, combining body observation and physical examination results, forming a physiological health background and nutritional clues, as foundational data for subsequent assessment, diagnosis, and Intervention (including necessary referrals).
459.when_to_use: Basic case information recording and preliminary assessment stage.
459.trigger: The interview or data provide height, weight / body shape information, or weight management is discussed and the existence of bodily problems confirmed.

409.skill_name: Assessing sleep and ruling out physiological factors
409.skill_description: Ask about the frequency and duration of insomnia, nighttime awakenings/dreams, and sleep schedule, and record daytime impacts (Decreased attention, fatigue). Verifying medical conclusions like 'no organic cause found yet', conducting medical factor screening when necessary, as the basis for physiological health and severity assessment.
409.when_to_use: When first to early counseling conducts medical factor screening, or during symptom assessment of depression/Anxiety presentations.
409.trigger: When the client reports insomnia or Declining sleep quality, impaired daytime functioning, or has had related physical examinations.

486.skill_name: Assessing appetite, weight, and nutritional status
486.skill_description: Learn in detail about recent appetite and eating patterns, quantifying the magnitude and time window of weight changes (such as dropping to 90 jin in two weeks), combining clues like low weight, low blood sugar, and fatigue to judge nutritional risk and physiological burden, as the basis for differential diagnosis, follow-up monitoring, and Intervention/referral.
486.when_to_use: When symptom assessment proceeds simultaneously and accompanying physiological symptoms and life-rhythm changes need attention; when the presenting complaint involves diet or weight.
486.trigger: When the client reports Decreased appetite, reduced eating, or weight changes; or experiences low weight, low blood sugar, and energy fluctuations.

337.skill_name: Clarifying and agreeing on counseling frequency, duration, and total sessions
337.skill_description: Explain to the client and jointly determine the frequency, single-session length, and estimated total number of counseling sessions, clarifying fixed times and locations when necessary (such as every Thursday afternoon, 50-60 minutes per session, 8-12 sessions total), and explaining that adjustments can follow progress, to form stable Anticipation and facilitate time management and decisions about continuing.
337.when_to_use: After counseling goals are clarified, entering the plan formulation and scheduling stage, or when formulating a counseling plan for the first time.
337.trigger: The client asks about follow-up arrangements; frequency, single-session duration, total number of sessions, and fixed times need to be settled so they can decide whether to continue.

379.skill_name: Plan the counseling process and each session's procedure by stage
379.skill_description: Divide the counseling process into stages and explain each stage's tasks and estimated sessions (such as 1-2 sessions for assessment and relationship building; 3-5 sessions for psychological help; session 6 for summary and closure), and clarify the basic structure of each session (opening review and jointly set agenda, closing homework assignment and follow-up agreement), introducing the planned methods and process when necessary, reducing uncertainty.
379.when_to_use: After the overall arrangement is preliminarily clarified, stage emphases and each session's procedure need to be further explained to facilitate implementation and tracking.
379.trigger: When the client wants to know the general content and stage tasks of each session, or feels uncertain and Anxiety about the subsequent process and pace.

427.skill_name: Clarify and confirm counseling frequency, duration, and fees
427.skill_description: Inform and confirm the frequency and single-session length of counseling (such as once a week, 45-50 minutes per session), combining with the estimated total sessions (such as 3-6 short-term sessions or a longer cycle), and explaining the institution's fee/free policy, helping the client form realistic Anticipation, coordinate time, and decide whether to continue.
427.when_to_use: After assessment and goals are clear, at the planning and arrangement stage before formal Intervention.
427.trigger: The client needs to clarify the schedule and commitment, or asks about specific matters such as the number of sessions, frequency, duration, and fees.

449.skill_name: Explain the counseling process and tasks by phase
449.skill_description: Divide the counseling process into several stages and explain the tasks and durations (such as sessions 1-2 intake assessment and preparation; sessions 3-6 adopting concrete techniques such as metacognition/cognitive behavioral; afterwards entering the consolidation and improvement/relapse-prevention stage), making the progress and goals clear, facilitating advancing and assessing by stage.
449.when_to_use: When formulating plans, needing to explain the overall process, stage goals, and Anticipated duration to the client.
449.trigger: The client needs to understand what is done at each stage and for how long, in order to form structured expectations and cooperate.

212.skill_name: Introduce and agree on the counseling method and rationale
212.skill_description: Explain the planned methods and principles to the client (such as rational emotive therapy, client-centered, Relaxation training, and ABC key points), introducing their effects and steps, and reaching agreement on whether to adopt them and how to cooperate, fostering informed consent and cooperative Anticipation.
212.when_to_use: The first session's assessment is complete, entering the plan negotiation and method selection stage.
212.trigger: When the client feels confused about 'how to change' or needs to understand the Intervention rationale and basis to decide whether to continue.

172.skill_name: Schedule counseling priorities and tasks by phase
172.skill_description: Explain the session focuses and tasks to the client by stage (such as sessions 1-2: information collection and relationship building; sessions 3-6: using techniques such as cognitive behavioral therapy to handle the distress; sessions 7-8: consolidation and ending), letting them grasp the path and rhythm and facilitating progress according to plan.
172.when_to_use: After scheduling, when consensus on the tasks and focuses of each stage needs to be reached.
172.trigger: When the client wants a clear counseling roadmap, stage tasks, and ways of advancing, to reduce uncertainty.

526.skill_name: Explain and negotiate the counseling setting and arrangements
526.skill_description: Clearly inform about the treatment setting and time frame (such as once a week, 50-60 minutes per session, an expected number of sessions), and negotiate the concrete time and place with the client, explaining fees and precautions where necessary, so that both parties can manage time and adjust plans.
526.when_to_use: After goals reach consensus, at the plan formulation and notification stage or before the end of the first session.
526.trigger: The client needs to know the specific frequency and duration, location and fees, or needs to schedule the next session.

354.skill_name: Assign between-session practice and adjust based on feedback
354.skill_description: After each session clarify the practice content and duration (such as 15-30 minutes daily), at the next session hear the completion status and confusions, and adjust the training plan and homework difficulty according to the feedback, forming a practice — feedback — optimization closed loop to raise the effect.
354.when_to_use: Assign homework at the end of each counseling session; review and adjust at the start of the next session.
354.trigger: The client feeds back difficulties or progress in practice (such as attention drifting, pain, emotional distress), and the plan needs optimizing.

508.skill_name: Set each session's structure and homework linkage
508.skill_description: Clarify the structure of each session: review the homework and the past week's situation at the opening and jointly set the current topic and goals; at the end, assign targeted homework and agree on the next follow-up, ensuring the continuity and traceability of the sessions.
508.when_to_use: After entering a regular cycle, when the structure of each session and homework linkage need to be standardized.
508.trigger: At the beginning and end of each session, continuity management of implementation, current topics, and next tasks is needed.

353.skill_name: Negotiate and set the frequency, duration, and fixed time slots
353.skill_description: Clarify and agree with the client on the session frequency and the length of each session (such as once a week, about 1 hour) and a fixed time slot (such as every Friday 13:00-14:00), raising implementation feasibility, facilitating scheduling, and stabilizing the rhythm of participation and assessment.
353.when_to_use: When formulating the counseling plan or when scheduling is needed at the end of a session.
353.trigger: When both parties' schedules allow and a fixed time needs to be determined; the client requests a clear frequency and time slot.

338.skill_name: Select and explain the counseling orientation and technique combination
338.skill_description: Confirm the main orientation and technique combination with the client (such as rational emotive therapy as primary, supplemented by solution-focused, relaxation/mindfulness, Socratic Questioning, interpersonal skills training, and Homework), explaining the basis for selection and Anticipated effects, reaching understanding and cooperation.
338.when_to_use: When formulating the counseling plan, needing to determine the Intervention path and technical framework.
338.trigger: When goals are set and the client raises questions about methods and procedures or informed consent needs to be formed.

215.skill_name: Developing staged plans based on the method
215.skill_description: Combined with orientations such as rational emotive therapy, refine the process into stages and tasks (such as the insight stage, the working-through stage, consolidation and ending), specify the focus and order of each stage, and guide the advancement of the intervention and the phased evaluations.
215.when_to_use: After the preliminary plan is drafted, when needing to outline the focus and sequence of each stage.
215.trigger: When methods are selected and specific and final goals are clear, needing staged advancement and Anticipation management.

363.skill_name: Clarify multi-module treatment frequency and schedule
363.skill_description: Concretely explain the frequency and arrangement of each module (such as individual therapy twice a week, family therapy once a week, group once a week), and after communication jointly confirm a feasible timetable; where necessary simultaneously explain fees and appointment/notification rules, facilitating cooperation and management.
363.when_to_use: After introducing the program structure, when the plan needs to be implemented into specific schedules and frequencies.
363.trigger: When the client/family asks about visit frequency or has concerns about time and administrative arrangements.

382.skill_name: Agree on phase adjustments and follow-up arrangements
382.skill_description: Gradually adjust the frequency with progress (such as lowering it to once every two weeks), and set follow-up nodes after the end (such as telephone / face-to-face visits at 1 month and 2 months), to consolidate changes, evaluate maintenance effects, and prevent recurrence.
382.when_to_use: Counseling enters the consolidation/termination stage, or at initial planning when a follow-up strategy needs to be agreed in advance.
382.trigger: Symptoms improve markedly, or there are concerns about reducing/ending counseling and inquiries about subsequent arrangements.

141.skill_name: Schedule post-counseling follow-up visits and tracking
141.skill_description: At the ending, formulate a return-visit and follow-up scheme (such as following up via WeChat or face-to-face at a certain period after the ending), understand adaptation and emotional changes, check the goal maintenance situation, where necessary provide support or adjust the scheme, consolidating the effect and preventing relapse.
