141.when_to_use: When counseling is basically ending and effects need consolidation and maintenance monitoring.
141.trigger: When goals are achieved and ending counseling is decided, follow-up return visits and follow-up points need to be agreed.

188.skill_name: Adjust the plan based on progress and arrange termination
188.skill_description: Adjust the initial plan according to progress and the client's wishes; when they propose that it can end, negotiate and arrange a summary session, review and consolidate gains, confirm results and follow-up arrangements, and promote the change's continuation and transfer outside sessions.
188.when_to_use: In the mid-to-late counseling stage, when reviewing progress or the client proposes adjustment / ending needs.
188.trigger: Distress is markedly relieved, goals are basically achieved, or the client clearly expresses a wish to end counseling.

237.skill_description: Clarify the stages of structured CBT and the focus of each session (such as session 1: conceptualization and goals; sessions 2-4: identifying and correcting irrational beliefs; sessions 5-8: behavioral correction; sessions 9-10: consolidation and relapse prevention), helping the client understand the treatment path and Anticipation.
237.when_to_use: After agreeing on goals with the client, when the overall treatment path and stage focuses need to be explained.
237.trigger: The client needs to understand the subsequent steps, methods, and the focus of each session to form structured expectations.

196.skill_name: Explain counseling frequency, session count, duration, and fees
196.skill_description: Explain to the client the counseling frequency, expected total number of sessions, and length of each session, and clarify the fee/free policy (such as once a week, about 10 sessions in total, 50-60 minutes per session, free throughout), so they can reasonably arrange time and resources and decide whether to continue.
196.when_to_use: After goals are clarified, when formulating the preliminary counseling plan and arrangements.
196.trigger: When the client needs to know the time and cost to decide whether to continue counseling.

392.skill_name: Informing and setting the total number of staged sessions
392.skill_description: At the planning stage, estimate and inform the staged or total number of sessions (such as 3-4 sessions or 5 sessions per stage), setting evaluation milestones and stage goals accordingly, enhancing predictability and commitment, and facilitating arrangement and decisions.
392.when_to_use: When formulating a preliminary counseling plan, needing to help the client form realistic expectations.
392.trigger: The client asks 'how many sessions are needed', or stage length needs to be clarified to guide execution and review.

236.skill_name: Dividing stages and previewing stage tasks
236.skill_description: Divide the counseling process into several stages and explain each stage's tasks (such as sessions 1-2: relationship building and goals; sessions 3-6: identifying and challenging Automatic thoughts; sessions 7-10: exploring beliefs and behavioral experiments; sessions 11-12: consolidation and summary), providing macro structure and pacing guidance.
236.when_to_use: When formulating the overall plan, used to clearly display the process and the focus of each stage.
236.trigger: The client wants to understand the roadmap, stage tasks, and the focus points of each stage.

439.skill_name: Assign between-session homework and practice plans
439.skill_description: Convert interventions into operable between-session tasks and exercises (such as recording distressing events and emotions, daily relaxation training, situational/interpersonal practice), agree on completion frequency and feedback methods, to consolidate changes within sessions and promote transfer.
439.when_to_use: At the end of the session or when making plans, when intersession consolidation and practice arrangements need to be clarified.
439.trigger: A need for continuous practice or monitoring of changes between sessions to support plan execution and effect evaluation.

489.skill_name: Explain the three-stage counseling process and key tasks
489.skill_description: Outline the three-stage counseling process and tasks: diagnostic assessment and relationship building; psychological help (introducing theory, identifying and correcting irrational beliefs, etc.); closure and consolidation (consolidating effects, Reinforcement education, ending the relationship), establishing shared Anticipation of the process and milestones.
489.when_to_use: When developing and explaining the counseling plan to the client.
489.trigger: The client needs to understand the overall process and staged tasks in order to cooperate and manage expectations.

500.skill_name: Explain the proposed method and its theoretical basis
500.skill_description: Explain to the client the main methods to be used and their theoretical basis (such as client-centered, rational emotive therapy and ABC theory), introducing their goals and mechanisms, so they understand and agree to the implementation plan, forming consistent Anticipation.
500.when_to_use: When formulating the counseling plan and needing to explain the plan content and basis before cooperation is reached.
500.trigger: When the client asks how counseling proceeds and its theoretical and methodological basis, or informed consent is needed.

347.skill_name: Clarify the counseling setting, rights and obligations, and sign the contract
347.skill_description: Explain the counseling setting and rules (session length, confidentiality principles and exceptions, etc.), clarify the rights and obligations of both parties (such as truthful information, completing homework, keeping to time, etc.), provide written explanations and complete the signing of informed consent/confidentiality agreement, establishing a cooperative contract and safety boundaries.
347.when_to_use: At the first session or plan-confirmation stage, when the setting and ethics need to be explained and contracting completed.
347.trigger: When the client has doubts about confidentiality and rules, is uneasy on the first visit, or is about to enter ongoing counseling.

153.skill_name: Explaining fee policies and charging arrangements
153.skill_description: Truthfully explain this counseling's fees and policies (such as on-campus counseling being free or the fee standards), helping the client decide whether to continue on an informed basis, and accordingly manage subsequent time and resources well, reducing economic concerns.
153.when_to_use: When formulating the plan for the first time and obtaining informed consent, administrative and resource information needs to be clarified.
153.trigger: When the client asks about fees or the institution requires informing in advance of the charging / free policy.

342.skill_name: Developing a graded exposure training plan
342.skill_description: Build a graded exposure hierarchy from easy to difficult based on the Anxiety level of fear situations, first conducting imaginal exposure/desensitization and rehearsal, clarifying the abandonment of safety behaviors and external attention training, then gradually implementing in-vivo exposure and assigning between-session homework, promoting the reduction of and adaptation to avoidant behaviors.
342.when_to_use: After cognitive reconstruction, when behavioral practice is still needed and systematic exposure training is to be carried out.
342.trigger: When the client shows obvious Anxiety and avoidance in specific situations and is willing to try graded exposure.

531.skill_name: Negotiate and clarify counseling goals and the plan
531.skill_description: After a preliminary understanding of the distress, negotiate with and confirm for the client near-term and long-term goals, discuss the methods and stage plans to be used, clarify the direction and focuses of this and subsequent sessions, and form a joint work contract and guidance.
531.when_to_use: From the early to middle part of the first session, after basic understanding and problem clarification are completed, or at stage transitions.
531.trigger: The client has stated the main problem and is willing to cooperate, and the work focus and path of the current stage need to be clarified, or the client asks 'what should be done next'.

530.skill_name: Explain the counseling process, setting, and schedule
530.skill_description: At the opening or early stage, clearly introduce the counseling process and stage tasks, explaining frequency, single-session length, total sessions, and fees, and clarifying the current session's tasks and subsequent steps, reducing uncertainty and casual narration, improving cooperation and efficiency.
530.when_to_use: At the structured explanation stage of the first or early sessions, or before this session ends when follow-up needs to be arranged.
530.trigger: When the client is unclear about the counseling purpose and process, actively asks about frequency, length, and fees, or needs to set the next appointment.

410.skill_name: Introducing counseling matters and basic rules
410.skill_description: At the start of the session, explain counseling matters and basic rules, including appointments, cooperation, and boundaries, so the client understands the session arrangement and interaction style, reducing uncertainty and resistance, laying the structure for subsequent assessment.
410.when_to_use: At the start of the first session or when beginning a new phase.
410.trigger: When new clients are unclear about the process, appear hesitant, or need informed explanation; when questions about cooperation rules are raised.

430.skill_name: Jointly agree on goals and plans and explain the methods
430.skill_description: After assessment and preliminary diagnosis, clarify with the client near-term and long-term goals, determine the intervention plan and the principles and procedures of the therapy to be used, and when necessary provide brief psychoeducation, so both parties reach agreement on tasks and methods.
430.when_to_use: After assessment is complete and before entering the counseling stage, or at the start of the second session.
430.trigger: A preliminary diagnosis and cause analysis have been formed; the client expresses motivation to change and seeks concrete methods.

476.skill_name: Explain the counseling matters, process, and the session's tasks
476.skill_description: At the first session, explain the precautions and rules, outline the steps of this session (such as registration, assessment, information collection, and preliminary analysis), arrange scale tests when necessary, helping the client understand the process and focus the narration.
476.when_to_use: The opening of the first session, used to establish common understanding and prepare for assessment.
476.trigger: When the client is unclear about the process and rules, waiting for guidance or asking about the current session's arrangement and tasks.

271.skill_name: Explain and confirm session frequency and duration
271.skill_description: Clarify the frequency of counseling and the length of a single session (such as once a week, 45-60 minutes); when necessary determine the next appointment time, helping the client understand the time framework, facilitating scheduling and ensuring punctual attendance and cooperation.
271.when_to_use: When establishing the treatment contract or the first structured explanation, plan implementation, and closing.
271.trigger: When the client asks about duration / frequency; or when schedules need confirmation or signs of time conflicts appear.

447.skill_name: Clarifying short-term and long-term counseling goals
447.skill_description: After assessment and conceptualization, clearly list the short-term and long-term goals of this stage, and confirm consensus with the client, making the direction and Anticipation concrete and achievable, guiding subsequent steps and priorities.
447.when_to_use: After completing initial assessment and conceptualization, when aligning direction and expectations.
447.trigger: When a preliminary judgment has been formed and it is time to unify counseling goals and Anticipated outcomes.

377.skill_name: Explain the methods, stage arrangement, and time pacing
377.skill_description: Explain the planned methods and stage tasks to the client, clarifying frequency, single-session length, and estimated total sessions, and outlining each stage's priorities, so they grasp the overall process and Anticipated path.
377.when_to_use: After the initial assessment is completed and preliminary goals are formed, or at the plan formulation stage.
377.trigger: When the client is unclear about frequency, length, or subsequent steps, needing structured explanation.

505.skill_name: Agreeing on the current session's content and steps
505.skill_description: After review, negotiate with the client to determine the current session's theme, tasks, and priorities, outlining steps and reaching shared Anticipation, improving focus and collaboration, reducing time wasted by casual narration.
505.when_to_use: After completing the review assessment, before formally entering the current session's topic.
505.trigger: When the content and goals of this discussion need to be jointly clarified, or the client's topics are scattered.

222.skill_name: Sign informed consent and explain the nature of counseling
222.skill_description: Completes informed consent with the client, explains the nature of counseling and basic arrangements, agrees on frequency and duration, ensures their informed choice, clarifies the structure and boundaries of this session.
222.when_to_use: At the setup stage of the first session or Evaluative session opening.
222.trigger: A new case visits for the first time, needing to reach agreement on frequency and duration.

231.skill_name: Conduct early psychoeducation to align understanding
231.skill_description: In the initial sessions, carry out necessary psychoeducation, helping the client understand the current distress and the focus and manner of counseling, raising cooperation and grasp of the process, and laying the foundation for goal formulation and technique use.
231.when_to_use: Synchronously with or after organizing the problem list, used to enhance understanding and cooperation.
231.trigger: When the client has insufficient understanding of the distress causes or counseling methods, having questions or Anxiety.

492.skill_name: Explaining the setting and confidentiality, completing consent and registration
492.skill_description: Guide filling in the registration form and signing the informed consent, explain both parties' responsibilities, rights, and obligations and confidentiality and its exceptions, clarify the setting and process, structure the session with standardized procedures, reduce doubts, and establish boundaries and expectations.
492.when_to_use: At the opening of the first Evaluative session or the setup stage before formally entering counseling.
492.trigger: At the first visit or when there are questions about process, privacy, and rights and responsibilities and boundaries need clarifying.

523.skill_name: Co-build the agenda and focus on the session's priority issues
523.skill_description: Agree with the client on the concrete content and focus of this session, rank priorities combined with the problem list, clarify goals and process, improving session efficiency and avoiding topic divergence.
523.when_to_use: After completing last week's review, when this session's agenda and priorities need to be set.
523.trigger: When the client raises multiple topics or concerns at the same time, needing focusing and prioritization.

298.skill_name: Outline the session's tasks and process and advance item by item
298.skill_description: At the opening, clarify the tasks to be completed in this session and their order (such as gathering information, preliminary analysis, organizing the problem list, and setting goals), making the exchange orderly and efficient and paving the way for subsequent arrangements.
298.when_to_use: At the start of the first session or before moving into the topic, when consensus on the scope and order of this session is needed.
298.trigger: When the client's narration is scattered, the focus unclear, or asking 'what are we mainly doing today'.

385.skill_name: Negotiate goals and plans and specify the therapy
385.skill_description: After assessment and testing, jointly agree with the client on the counseling goals and plan, and clarify the therapy to be adopted, making the session's direction and methods clear and consistent, raising cooperation and a sense of expectation.
385.when_to_use: In the second half of the first session or after the preliminary assessment is complete.
385.trigger: After assessments such as SAS/SDS are completed and the follow-up path and methods need to be clarified.

355.skill_description: Work with the client to refine vague expectations into concrete, operable, and measurable goals, clarify the behavioral standards and scenario boundaries, as the basis for intervention arrangement and evaluation, and make necessary realistic adjustments.
355.when_to_use: At the end of the first session or in the early stage, after psychoeducation, when goals and evaluation criteria need to be clarified.
355.trigger: When the client's goal statements are vague or idealized, hard to measure and operationalize.

521.skill_name: Complete informed consent and clarify rights and obligations
521.skill_description: Before counseling begins, explain both parties' responsibilities, rights, and obligations, emphasize confidentiality and boundaries, obtain the client's consent and establish a clear cooperation framework, improving transparency and safety.
521.when_to_use: Before the first session begins or during the opening phase.
521.trigger: When visiting for the first time, unclear about the counseling process, rights and responsibilities, or asking about relevant regulations.

312.skill_description: Clearly inform the counseling frequency, single-session length, estimated total sessions, and fee situation (such as free on campus), helping the client form realistic Anticipation and facilitating time and resource arrangements.
312.when_to_use: In the first session structuring stage or when formulating a preliminary counseling plan.
312.trigger: When the client asks about length, number of sessions, or fees, or has not yet learned the specific arrangements.

339.skill_name: Explain and implement the session frequency and pace
339.skill_description: State and confirm the session frequency, the length of each session, and the total number of sessions per stage (such as once daily later changing to once weekly), ensuring both parties agree on the pace and rhythm to facilitate cooperation.
339.when_to_use: When establishing the counseling plan or before the end of the first session.
339.trigger: When a schedule needs to be arranged, the client asks about frequency/number of sessions, or there is a time conflict needing coordination.

479.skill_description: At the start of each stage, explain the current period's tasks and goals (such as building relationships, Information gathering, identifying beliefs, etc.), aligning expectations and evaluation standards, keeping sessions focused and facilitating process evaluation.
479.when_to_use: At the start of each phase or topic change.
479.trigger: When preparing to enter a new stage (such as assessment, Intervention, or consolidation).

422.skill_name: Clarifying the current session's goals and tasks
422.skill_description: At the beginning of the session, unify the theme and tasks of this session (such as intake consensus, understanding the situation, preliminary assessment), define the focus and boundaries, avoid divergence, and lay the foundation for the subsequent plan.
422.when_to_use: At the first service or the start of each session.
422.trigger: When first taking on a case or topics are not yet clear, and the conversation starts to scatter.

170.skill_name: Clarify the tasks and methods of the assessment phase
170.skill_description: Focus the 1st-2nd sessions on information collection and relationship building, explain that intake interviews and assessments will be carried out, define the main problem and do preliminary analysis, avoiding topic divergence.
170.when_to_use: At the opening and agenda confirmation of the first two sessions of the Evaluative session.
170.trigger: When the client is unclear about the assessment priorities and process or expects immediate Intervention.

415.skill_name: Explain rights, responsibilities, and confidentiality; establish boundaries
415.skill_description: Explain the responsibilities, rights, and obligations of the help-seeker and the counselor, emphasize the confidentiality principle and its exceptions, complete the consent procedure when necessary, and let the client begin cooperating within informed and safe boundaries.
415.when_to_use: At the structured explanation stage of the initial session or when formulating a counseling plan.
415.trigger: When the client raises questions about rights, confidentiality, or boundaries, or appears uneasy.

490.skill_name: Introduce the counseling phases and priorities
490.skill_description: Outline the staged counseling process (such as assessment and relationship building - psychological help - Consolidation and termination), explaining each stage's tasks and transitions, helping the client understand the overall structure and Anticipation.
490.when_to_use: At the first session or when explaining the counseling plan.
490.trigger: When the client is unclear about the overall process and subsequent arrangements or feels uneasy about progress.

315.skill_name: Explaining counseling duration, frequency, and fees
315.skill_description: Explain to the client the time and frequency (such as once a week, 50 minutes per session), the estimated number of sessions, and the fee policy (such as free at school), so they understand the pace, investment, and commitment.
315.when_to_use: At the start of the Evaluative session or when formulating the plan.
315.trigger: When the client asks about length, frequency, fees, or is unclear about arrangements.

393.skill_name: Introduce the principles and process of rational emotive / cognitive therapy
393.skill_description: Use plain language to introduce the core views and ABC framework of rational-emotive/cognitive therapy, explaining the working style, steps, and precautions, helping the client understand key points of cooperation and align Anticipation.
393.when_to_use: The first or early sessions, after assessment and goal negotiation, used for method explanation.
393.trigger: When the client is unclear about methods and process, asking 'how does it work/is it effective' or needing to reach agreement.

132.skill_name: Announce and negotiate the session theme and agenda
132.skill_description: Points out this session's theme and tasks, briefly explains the process and time allocation, and solicits the client's consent and willingness to participate, ensuring both parties reach consensus on the agenda and methods.
132.when_to_use: Before shifting from Listening to the Intervention focus or at the opening of each session.
132.trigger: When the client's narration is scattered, unclear about the current session's arrangement, or repeatedly shows Automatic thoughts needing focus.

387.skill_name: Assign self-help/homework and agree on a review
387.skill_description: At the end of the session, assign specific actionable homework (such as belief scoring, relaxation or communication practice), clarify the recording method and practice frequency, and agree on the next review arrangement, forming a session-homework-feedback closed loop.
387.when_to_use: At the end stage of each session, used to consolidate learning and arrange subsequent steps.
387.trigger: When this session's goal is achieved and practice needs to be transferred to daily situations, or the client asks about post-session arrangements.

397.skill_name: Filling in the registration/interview form to start information collection
397.skill_description: Arranges and guides the filling of counseling registration and interview forms, standardized collection of basic information and chief complaint, starts the assessment process, ensuring data completeness and facilitating later diagnosis and planning.
397.when_to_use: The start of intake and information gathering at the first interview.
397.trigger: When basic information and chief complaints need to be systematically obtained and files and session records established.

306.skill_name: Use intake conversation to focus content and scope
306.skill_description: After data collection at the first session, define the content and scope of this and subsequent sessions, clarify that intake dialogue and preliminary conceptualization will center on the main distress, avoiding general talk and going off topic.
306.when_to_use: The early assessment segment from the start of the first session.
306.trigger: When basic situation and chief complaints have been obtained and the topic scope and methods need to be clarified.

277.skill_name: Introduces and negotiates the use of methods such as CBT/ACT
277.skill_description: After the initial assessment, briefly introduce the concepts, principles, and procedures of the method to be used (such as CBT/ACT), provide necessary psychoeducation, and jointly decide with the client whether to adopt it, clarifying the intervention path and cooperation method.
277.when_to_use: After completing the preliminary assessment, preparing to enter the Intervention stage.
277.trigger: When the client is unfamiliar with counseling methods, asks how they proceed, or needs orientation and procedures clarified.

197.skill_name: Introduce the treatment method framework and structured process
197.skill_description: Explain the principles, overall goals, and operational process of the methods used (such as CBT/DBT), outlining stage arrangements and transition points, jointly formulating target homework when necessary, to gain cooperation and align Anticipation.
197.when_to_use: The structured explanation of the first session, or the pre-treatment phase.
197.trigger: When the client is unclear about the treatment methods and overall arrangements, about to enter formal treatment.

127.skill_description: At the close, assign post-session tasks, specify the concrete practice and frequency, and set reminders (such as an alarm clock, daily reading), explaining how it will be reviewed and applied next time, consolidating what was learned in the session.
127.when_to_use: When the session ends or a stage concludes.
127.trigger: When this discussion is completed and the content needs to be turned into daily practice and specific tasks.

137.skill_name: Reviewing homework and determining this session's focus accordingly
137.skill_description: In the session, reviews last week's homework completion, discusses gains and difficulties, and based on this jointly decides this session's key problems and goals, enhancing continuity and targeting.
137.when_to_use: At the opening or middle of each session, before and after the agenda is set.
137.trigger: When the client brings homework records or reports execution difficulties, and themes need to be integrated and focused.

366.skill_name: Explain confidentiality principles, exceptions, and time settings
366.skill_description: In the early session introduces counseling matters, clarifies confidentiality and confidentiality exception principles, and explains the time setting and pace, enabling both parties to conduct the session under clear boundaries and rules.
366.when_to_use: At the beginning stage of sessions 1-2, before formal communication.
366.trigger: Entering the session-process preparation stage, when the client has concerns about privacy and time arrangements.

345.skill_name: Exploring Anticipation and explaining CBT to reach consensus
345.skill_description: Ask about the client's Anticipation for counseling, introduce the key points and working style of CBT, solicit feedback, and jointly determine counseling goals and session frequency, aligning both sides' understanding of the process and arrangements.
345.when_to_use: The structured components of the first session.
345.trigger: When agreement on the process is needed, or counseling goals and frequency, orientation and expectations need to be clarified.

433.skill_name: Assign recording-type homework to support subsequent assessment
433.skill_description: Before the end of the session, assign record-type homework (such as an event-emotion-cognition-behavior log / a thought-and-emotion record form / a counseling diary), explaining the filling-in method and the purpose, providing a basis for the next analysis and practice.
433.when_to_use: At the closing stage of the first or early sessions, when entering practice and monitoring.
433.trigger: When troubles need to be systematically organized and emotion-cognition patterns monitored, and the client is willing to do homework.

185.skill_name: Stating and confirming the confidentiality agreement
185.skill_description: At the initial visit, clarify the confidentiality principle, exceptions, and information-protection methods, respond to concerns and confirm consent, enhancing safety and trust, creating conditions for genuine disclosure and effective assessment.
185.when_to_use: Early in the first session, before formal exchange begins.
185.trigger: When the client has concerns about privacy and information use, directly asking about conversation boundaries.

210.skill_name: Arrange and administer psychological tests and feed back results
210.skill_description: At the initial session, arrange and implement tests such as SAS/SDS/SCL-90, obtain quantitative information and feed back the results, combined with preliminary analysis to support negotiation of goals and plans, improving focus and operability.
210.when_to_use: In the first or early assessment stage, when symptoms need quantifying to support a preliminary diagnosis.
210.trigger: When needing to assess the degree of Anxiety, depression, etc., or the client wants objective feedback.

421.skill_description: Through continuous Questioning, review specific situations, sequentially marking the trigger event, Automatic thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and outcomes/others' feedback, verbally summarizing or presenting 'this is a cycle' with tables/diagrams, highlighting maintaining factors and mutual Reinforcement, to locate subsequent Intervention.
421.when_to_use: At the early stage of assessment and case conceptualization, when the client describes distress but lacks a clear pattern, needing to present the maintaining vicious cycle and locate Intervention points.
421.trigger: When repeatedly reporting Anxiety, insomnia, Decreased efficiency, or interpersonal conflicts, and self-reporting 'getting worse/caught in a cycle', and can provide one specific situation.

199.skill_name: Explaining and consolidating the 'thoughts cause emotions' relationship
199.skill_description: Use structured dialogue to distinguish events, Automatic thoughts, and emotions, demonstrating and asking the client to restate in their own words that 'thoughts cause emotions', clarifying causality, laying the foundation for subsequent cycle mapping and Intervention.
199.when_to_use: At the initial or early session's psychoeducation and case conceptualization stage, when a common language and model understanding need to be established.
199.trigger: When narrating events, the client is obviously low in mood and confused in thinking, or is puzzled about the causes of their distress.

512.skill_name: Clarifying problem behaviors-emotions-outcomes and locating re-trigger points
512.skill_description: First define 'problem behaviors' in observable terms, locating the precipitating events; then link the Automatic thoughts, emotions, and behaviors at the time, marking consequences and new re-trigger points, visually presenting the consequence link and cycle maintenance.
512.when_to_use: When building the ABC / circular chain, when the C (emotion/behavior) and functional impact need to be clarified, or when starting a review of a recent problem behavior.
512.trigger: The client reports strong emotions or impairment in functioning such as study and interpersonal relations; or can recall one clear episode/conflict scene and asks 'Why is it like this'.

466.skill_name: Drawing the circular maintenance chain of the problem
466.skill_description: Based on the client's narrative, link situations, Automatic thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and outcomes into a circular maintenance chain, highlighting the relationship of 'outcomes in turn Reinforcing beliefs/re-triggering', providing a panoramic view for Intervention positioning.
466.when_to_use: At the Evaluative session and case conceptualization stage, after current symptoms, situations, and behavior patterns have been collected.
466.trigger: When situations like communication difficulties, late submissions/being criticized repeatedly appear, accompanied by fixed interpretations and reactions like Anxiety and avoidance.

467.skill_name: Determining interruption points and drafting initial cognitive/behavioral routes
467.skill_description: Select severable key connection points on the circular chain, preliminarily agreeing on cognitive or behavioral paths, such as identifying-assessing-testing Automatic thoughts, or designing behavioral attempts like proactive communication/sticking to the original plan, to break the maladaptive cycle.
467.when_to_use: After the maintenance chain has been sorted out and before counseling goals and a plan are formulated, or when the model needs to be translated into specific strategies.
467.trigger: The loop shows cognitive bias and avoidance jointly maintaining the problem, and the client is willing to try change or is about to face a stimulus situation.

399.skill_name: Assigning emotion and thought record homework
399.skill_description: Arrange daily recording of emotions at different times and their causes, and in the Thought record sheet, fill in time/situation, Automatic thoughts, corresponding emotions and outcomes, or record multiple similar situations within a week, systematically collecting loop data.
399.when_to_use: After the first chain analysis and in the intervals between sessions, as data collection and practice for early assessment and conceptualization.
399.trigger: Emotional fluctuation is marked or automatic thoughts are hard to notice in daily life; there are multiple similar interpersonal / learning situations whose commonalities need comparing.

475.skill_name: Using recorded materials to build a situation-thought-emotion-behavior loop diagram
475.skill_description: Take the concrete events recorded by the client in the homework as clues, and sort out in sequence the situation, the automatic thoughts at that moment, and the corresponding emotional and behavioral responses, presenting the interaction of elements and possible loop junctions in combination with the conceptualization chart.
475.when_to_use: The assessment and case conceptualization stage, or when reviewing specific situations such as discomfort in the study room.
475.trigger: The client can recall and describe the situation, emotions, and thoughts at the time, and is willing to cooperate with recording and diagrammatic presentation.

380.skill_name: Select typical high-frequency events for cross-sectional analysis
380.skill_description: From the chief complaint and homework, screen out events with high frequency, large impact, and long duration, mark item by item the situation, automatic thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and consequences, outline the circular chain and maintenance mechanisms, and locate intervention entry points.
380.when_to_use: At the case conceptualization stage, when needing to identify negative cycles and actionable Intervention points.
380.trigger: The client repeatedly narrates similar situations with marked distress, and can provide concrete narratives or typical statements.

327.skill_name: Explain emotional distress using the ABC framework
327.skill_description: Use the client's specific experience to demonstrate the A (event) - B (belief) - C (emotion / behavior) relationship, clarify that distress comes from the interpretation of the event rather than the event itself, and align the counseling goals and the direction of intervention.
327.when_to_use: The first assessment feedback and conceptualization-launch stage, used to build a shared understanding of the problem mechanism.
327.trigger: The client attributes distress directly to events, or is confused about the source of emotions, showing absolutist expressions.

158.skill_name: Categorizing case materials as A/B/C and organizing them structurally
158.skill_description: Based on the client's narrative, map the material onto ABC elements: identifying the inducing event A, defining the current belief B, and the emotional/behavioral outcome C, depicting the causal chain accordingly and laying the foundation for drawing the circular chain.
158.when_to_use: After completing the preliminary data collection, when the material needs to be structurally organized with ABC and understanding aligned.
158.trigger: Concrete clues about the event, thoughts, emotions, and behavior are provided, making it convenient to categorize them by A/B/C.

229.skill_name: Using the three-column form to record situation-thought-emotion
229.skill_description: Assign daily immediate filling of the three-column table when negative emotions arise, recording situations, Automatic thoughts, and emotion ratings, systematically tracking loop nodes, providing a basis for identifying patterns and comparing changes before and after Intervention.
229.when_to_use: From the early to middle Intervention period, to track thought-emotion patterns and situation triggers, and prepare for cognitive restructuring.
229.trigger: When negative emotions or automatic thoughts appear and structured recording and awareness practice are needed.

183.skill_name: Conduct cognitive restructuring with thought records
183.skill_description: Record events, automatic thoughts, and evidence in the three-column / five-column table, generate a more balanced alternative interpretation, and compare the changes in emotion scores and behavioral intentions before and after, so as to break the negative cognition-emotion-behavior cycle.
183.when_to_use: After identifying negative Automatic thoughts, at the stage of needing to test their evidence and form alternative thoughts.
183.trigger: In specific events, strong negative emotion ratings and pessimistic interpretations appear, and the client is willing to try cognitive alternatives.

275.skill_name: Assigning and guiding the RET self-help form to record A-B-C and irrational beliefs
275.skill_description: Explain the RET self-help form and require recording specific events (A) and irrational cognitions (B) when negative emotions arise, attempting to write reasonable alternatives, providing material for identifying maintaining factors and attribution correction.
275.when_to_use: After the first session and in the early conceptualization stage, as extension materials and exercises for homework.
275.trigger: When negative emotions appear frequently and self-awareness of one's own thinking is insufficient, or samples are insufficient and continuous recording is needed.

419.skill_name: Reviews and corrects the RET self-help form to revise the cognitive chain
419.skill_description: Check the self-help form entries in subsequent sessions, distinguishing events from beliefs, identifying new irrational beliefs, and Reinforcing reasonable alternative understanding, completing the case's event-belief-emotion/behavior-outcome chain.
419.when_to_use: At the next session or periodic review, used to evaluate homework effects and deepen circular conceptualization.
419.trigger: When the self-help form shows new erroneous cognitions or maladaptive habits, with still tense Anxiety or causal attribution bias.

348.skill_name: Specify and quantify symptoms and functional impact
348.skill_description: Around emotions, physiology, cognition, and behaviors, probe item by item and record, such as insomnia/poor sleep, appetite changes, decreased attention and memory, Social avoidance, decreased Learning efficiency, etc., clarifying frequency, duration, and severity, and marking the scope of impact on Learning, relationships, and daily life, to judge clinical significance and Intervention priority.
348.when_to_use: In the initial/current-state assessment stage, when the general chief complaint needs to be refined into quantifiable symptom and functioning information.
348.trigger: When the client mentions clues like 'feeling terrible/poor sleep/difficulty concentrating/not wanting to socialize/Declining grades/Reduced interest'.

451.skill_name: Refine and quantify the symptom list and timeline
451.skill_description: Guide the client to describe emotional, physiological, and behavioral symptoms in concrete words (such as Anxiety, insomnia, poor appetite, easy crying, inability to focus on things, numbness/chilliness all over), and clarifying onset time and duration (such as the past month/two weeks), quantifying frequency and intensity, while recording the impact on daily functioning, forming an assessable checklist.
451.when_to_use: The initial segment of presenting-complaint collection and symptom assessment, when the scope, timeline, and severity of the symptoms need to be defined.
451.trigger: When only broadly describing recent distress or lacking time, frequency, and intensity information; when describing specific experiences like 'Repression discomfort' or 'blank mind'.

240.skill_description: Around Learning, Work, relationships, and daily life, probe impaired manifestations and frequency item by item, concretizing such as having no friends at school, Loneliness, Decreased attention, low Work efficiency, impatience with colleagues, repeatedly contacting the other party, decreased Learning efficiency, Sleep disturbed, etc., clarifying the scope and degree of impairment, to judge clinical significance and Intervention priority.
240.when_to_use: Before initial assessment and goal priority determination, and at periodic reassessment follow-ups of functional changes.
240.trigger: When mentioning functional clues like declining academic focus, Social avoidance, disordered routine, Decreased work efficiency, or interpersonal conflicts.

257.skill_name: Detailing presenting symptoms and risk signals
257.skill_description: Around the client's self-report, record in detail concrete manifestations such as depressed mood, easy irritability, unwillingness to communicate, indifference, unfocused attention, and self-injury/suicide ideation, and mark duration and intensity, while supplementing physiological clues like sleep and appetite, providing a basis for clinical assessment and risk judgment.
257.when_to_use: At the chief complaint collection and symptom assessment stage, when the symptom scope, features, and potential risks need to be clarified.
257.trigger: When statements like 'inferiority, unwilling to communicate with others, easily irritated, cutting arms' appear, or reports of continued low mood for the past two weeks, headaches, skipping classes, etc.

281.skill_name: Record presenting symptoms and functional-impact cues
281.skill_description: Guide around the chief complaint and record duration (such as two months), emotional and physiological symptoms (restlessness, Decreased attention, poor sleep and appetite, etc.), combining with impacts on Learning, relationships, and activity participation (such as being unable to participate in cultural and sports activities, low Learning efficiency, distant relationships), and incorporating related major event clues (such as fainting, medical visits) to assess clinical significance.
281.when_to_use: Information collection and history-of-present-illness inquiry in the diagnostic assessment stage, when the chief complaint and its functional consequences need to be clarified.
281.trigger: Mentions restricted activities, affected learning, interpersonal problems, or clues that persistent worry and repeated thinking affect life.

324.skill_description: Structurally ask and record by four categories — emotion, cognition, behavior, physiology — such as Anxiety/loss, catastrophizing/black-and-white thinking/overgeneralization/blaming, social Withdrawal and avoidance, rapid heartbeat/sweating/Decreased appetite/poor sleep, etc., while organizing the frequency, severity, and recent changes of core depression- and Anxiety-related symptoms, establishing a symptom checklist.
324.when_to_use: At the first assessment and subsequent follow-ups, when systematically organizing the chief complaint and establishing the symptom spectrum and severity baseline.
324.trigger: When the client describes changes in emotions, thoughts, behaviors, and bodily reactions, or mentions Low mood, poor sleep, Anxiety with palpitations, etc.

148.skill_name: Assess duration, severity, and functional impairment
148.skill_description: Probe symptom onset and duration (such as in the past month/less than two weeks), frequency and intensity, specifically recording the impact on Learning efficiency, sleep, daytime fatigue, and attention, and simultaneously screening urgent risks like strong suicide thoughts, to determine clinical severity, Intervention urgency, and priority.
148.when_to_use: At the initial diagnosis and risk assessment stage, or after clarifying symptom content, when the course and severity need to be defined.
148.trigger: When significant functional decline appears (such as not going out for several consecutive days), strong suicide thoughts, or reports of poor sleep in the past month, Decreased efficiency, and other clues.

334.skill_name: Detail the chief complaint symptoms, onset time, and functional impact
334.skill_description: Around sadness, distress, restlessness, insomnia, inability to concentrate, low Learning efficiency, etc. appearing after painful events, probe frequency and duration in detail; inventory symptom clusters like mania, depression, and auditory hallucinations when necessary, and clarify impacts on functional areas like Learning, relationships, and thoughts of dropping out, forming a clinical description.
334.when_to_use: At the assessment stage, when needing to form a clear clinical picture and determine Intervention priorities.
334.trigger: When the client actively states recent painful events, or generalizes distress with vague terms like 'very anxious/very annoyed'.

423.skill_description: Around Learning and Work efficiency, task completion, social participation, and daily routine/self-care, ask item by item, recording 'unwilling to go to school, rarely communicating, not participating in cultural and sports activities, barely keeping up in class with poor results, feeling Loneliness', etc., noting 'not yet affected' when necessary, to determine the scope and degree of functional impairment and Intervention priority.
423.when_to_use: After the chief complaint narrative, when entering functional impact assessment and Intervention priority ordering.
423.trigger: When mentioning functional clues like decreased Learning efficiency, Reduced socializing, disordered routine, considering a leave of absence, or unwillingness to return to the dormitory.

223.skill_description: Regarding the symptoms and functional impacts already presented, ask further and quantify the severity, occurrence frequency, and duration (such as 'the past two weeks', 'more than twenty times a day', 'only sleeping 5-6 hours'), concretizing vague statements, facilitating judging severity and formulating intervention priorities.
223.when_to_use: After a preliminary understanding of the chief complaint, when it is necessary to objectify symptom features and define severity and course.
223.trigger: When there are only label-like descriptions lacking duration/frequency/intensity information, or reports of long-term insomnia, emotional fluctuations, etc.

373.skill_name: Guide concretization of the chief complaint and symptom presentation
373.skill_description: Use open-ended Questioning and Listening to prompt the client to detail in their own words the emotional, physiological, and behavioral experiences of the past two weeks/past month (such as Depression, Anxiety, nervousness, insomnia, hand trembling, etc.), making the chief complaint concrete and recordable, laying the foundation for further detailed and quantitative assessment.
373.when_to_use: At the first-stage assessment of the chief complaint and symptom presentation, or early in relationship building when a comprehensive understanding is needed.
373.trigger: When only vaguely describing 'uncomfortable/tense/emotionally unstable', etc., making it difficult to focus on chief complaint details.

343.skill_name: Clarifying the Anxiety themes and symptom composition
343.skill_description: Around Anxiety-related chief complaints, probe emotional intensity, situations of occurrence, and core worries, and structurally record health Anxiety's disease preoccupation, somatic symptoms, distorted beliefs and related behaviors, as well as Social anxiety's manifestations in social situations — tension, avoiding eye contact/lowering voice/remaining Silent, etc. — and their duration in years, summarizing the emotional, physiological, and behavioral dimensions and severity.
343.when_to_use: At the preliminary assessment of the chief complaint, when defining the specific content of emotional and cognitive symptoms, or involving health/Social anxiety.
343.trigger: When the client self-reports Anxiety, worries about the future or Self-doubt; reports Social tension, worrying about losing control and avoidance, etc.

259.skill_name: Clarifying the presenting complaint and core distress
259.skill_description: Use open and focused questions to guide the client to explain in concrete statements the reason for the visit, the core distress, and the scenes where it occurs, clarify the start time and duration, and optionally use subjective satisfaction to elicit emotional experiences and help-seeking goals, forming a clear problem focus and assessment direction.
259.when_to_use: At the beginning of the initial assessment stage, when the chief complaint, distress situations, and session goals need to be clarified.
259.trigger: When only vaguely expressing 'poor interpersonal relationships/very nervous', or when the chief complaint and timeline have not yet been actively explained.

506.skill_name: Assess avoidance behaviors and social-function impairment
506.skill_description: Probe and record the scope of avoidant behaviors, their duration in years, and their impact on Learning/Work/life, exemplifying avoiding taking the bus alone and distant places, frequent mistakes at Work, unwillingness to socialize with others, avoiding group activities, taking a leave of absence, etc., comprehensively judging the degree of functional impairment and Intervention priority.
506.when_to_use: After the chief complaint symptoms are clarified, when functional impact and avoidance patterns need to be assessed to determine priorities.
506.trigger: When mentioning clues like long-term avoidance, affected tasks, or significant functional limitations (such as not attending classes, taking a leave of absence).

468.skill_name: Assess learning-function impairment and objective indicators
468.skill_description: For concretizing Learning functional impairment — manifestations, frequency, and situations of attention, memory, and classroom efficiency — recording objective indicators (number of failed courses, accumulated credits, whether at the edge of dropping out, etc.) and preserved functions (such as still participating in competitions), and combining with subjective feelings to define scope and severity.
468.when_to_use: When probing the functional impact of the chief complaint or determining functional baselines and Intervention priorities.
468.trigger: When academic clues appear such as poor attention in class, reduced efficiency, failing multiple courses, teachers suggesting a leave of absence, skipping classes.

394.skill_name: Observe and record mental status and overt behaviors
394.skill_description: Throughout the session, observe appearance, grooming, emotions, speech, behaviors, and thinking/perception, such as a tired-looking face, Low mood/Anxiety, clear speech or clear logic, repeatedly rubbing hands, tears and sobbing, very low voice, as objective corroboration of self-report, refining clinical judgment.
394.when_to_use: Mental state observation conducted alongside the complaint assessment; applicable at both initial diagnosis and follow-up.
394.trigger: When visible emotional and behavioral cues appear while entering the room and during the conversation, or the reaction is marked when sensitive topics are touched on.

361.skill_name: Assess functional impairment and check for high-risk behaviors
361.skill_description: Systematically ask about the chief complaint's impact on Learning, family, and social functioning, clarifying impairments like school refusal/leaves of absence; simultaneously probe the frequency, methods, most recent timing of self-injury/suicide thoughts and behaviors, and whether medical treatment was received, distinguishing current from past, to determine severity and Intervention priority.
361.when_to_use: At the initial assessment and when determining Intervention priorities, and continuously monitoring risk and functional changes during follow-ups.
361.trigger: When clues appear like hindered Learning, family conflicts, or self-injury/suicide-related behaviors and handling records.

406.skill_name: Suicide risk screening and graded recording
406.skill_description: Directly yet sensitively screen for suicidal thoughts, their persistence and concrete plans, quantify the frequency of ideation and the most recent time, distinguish fleeting thoughts from plans with a scheme; at the same time record protective beliefs and motivational inhibiting factors and the original words, and determine the risk level and whether urgent handling is needed.
406.when_to_use: In the chief complaint severity assessment and risk screening segment, or when significant depression/collapse and negative remarks appear.
406.trigger: When the client reports life Meaninglessness, with suicide intent/thoughts, self-injury thoughts, or despair expressions.

178.skill_name: Quantify mood and distress with 0-10 ratings
178.skill_description: Use a 0-10 subjective distress/pain rating; ask the client to rate their mood/state at present and at the last session and compare them, recording the values (e.g., 10/10), to quantify severity, fluctuation trends, and intervention effect tracking.
178.when_to_use: At the start of each session or topic transitions, or when symptom changes and efficacy need monitoring.
178.trigger: When the current mood needs to be objectified or the client reports emotional / symptom fluctuations.

519.skill_name: Assessing the impact of insomnia on daytime functioning
519.skill_description: Probe the impact of insomnia on daytime mental state, fatigue and drowsiness, attention and emotions (tension, distress, panic), recording concrete impaired manifestations like 'drowsy in class, unable to hear the teacher clearly, not participating in group activities, Declining grades', to assess Learning or social functioning impact and Intervention priority.
519.when_to_use: When the chief complaint involves sleep problems or it is necessary to assess the actual impact of the problem on study/social life.
519.trigger: When the client reports daytime fatigue, poor mental state, Insufficient motivation, declining grades, or skipping classes to nap, etc.

294.skill_name: Open-ended inquiry into the presenting complaint and symptoms
294.skill_description: Through open-ended Questioning and Listening, guide the client to freely narrate emotional, physiological, and behavioral distress (such as interpersonal Withdrawal, Low mood, tense insomnia, palpitations and sweaty hands, mistakes in problem-solving, etc.), capturing core pain points and subjective experiences, as material for subsequent concretization and quantitative assessment.
294.when_to_use: At the chief complaint and present illness history collection and relationship-building stage of the first session, when problem inquiry is launched.
294.trigger: When the client starts talking about exam Anxiety and pain, or finds it hard to express their symptoms and distress clearly.

165.skill_name: Clarifying onset time and precipitating events
165.skill_description: Ask when the symptoms began and the direct triggers, record key time points and situations (time, place, relevant people, and feelings at the time), and establish a timeline and preliminary associations between events and reactions, providing a starting point for course sorting and conceptualization.
165.when_to_use: In the interview on the course and triggers, when the baseline and starting point of the problem's occurrence need to be locked, or a timeline established at the initial assessment stage.
165.trigger: The client mentions a clear time point or specific event; timeline expressions such as 'since that incident', 'the recent two weeks', or 'after entering school' appear.

484.skill_description: Sort out in chronological order the evolution from the activating event to changes in emotion, sleep, appetite, and functioning, recording the duration, stage-wise intensification/remission, and whether it has generalized, forming a clear course map, supporting diagnosis and case conceptualization.
484.when_to_use: After identifying triggers or before sorting out the illness course and conceptualization, when needing to integrate the time dimension and change trajectory.
484.trigger: When the narrative shows time clues like 'the past two months', 'worsening/improvement', 'after this event', or clues are scattered and changes unclear, needing systematic integration.

454.skill_name: Confirming recent precipitating events and situations
454.skill_description: Clarify and record recent trigger events and environmental situations, keeping time, place, related people, and feelings at the time, forming an event-emotion/behavior chain, to grasp the relationship between triggers and the worsening of current distress.
454.when_to_use: At the course-sorting stage of the first session or when symptoms suddenly worsen, used to trace back triggering factors.
454.trigger: After the client mentions a specific event, emotions or behavior change obviously, describing 'suddenly worse', 'the most recent worsening'.

374.skill_name: Track the evolution of the course and phase changes
374.skill_description: Ask about intensity and fluctuations at different stages, clarifying patterns of worsening and improvement, whether generalization occurs, and functional impact, recording stage-wise changes to depict the evolution trajectory and support diagnosis and conceptualization.
374.when_to_use: When needing to judge the illness course and change patterns, identify trigger and alleviating factors, or form a stage-wise assessment.
374.trigger: The client describes 'sometimes severe, sometimes mild', a recent marked worsening, or a significant change in behavior patterns.

356.skill_description: Identify and record problem-related inducing events and aggravating factors, combining emotional and behavioral responses, distinguishing inducing from maintaining mechanisms, clarifying their link with symptom fluctuations, for subsequent conceptualization and Intervention design.
356.when_to_use: At the stage of exploring etiological clues and trigger factors, or before entering case conceptualization.
356.trigger: The client mentions that after a specific event the symptoms markedly worsened, avoidance began, or emotional-behavioral escalation occurred.

329.skill_name: Listing high-frequency trigger clues and topics
329.skill_description: Focus on repeatedly triggering clues, recording words or topics that trigger strong emotional reactions along with their frequency and environment, forming a trigger list, providing a basis for subsequent Intervention and early-warning mechanisms.
329.when_to_use: After the timeline is initially established, when needing to further clarify stable trigger clues and high-risk topics.
329.trigger: The client reports strong emotional reactions upon hearing specific words or topics.

322.skill_name: Constructing a course timeline and changes
322.skill_description: Sort out the starting point, duration, and changes over time, record nodes such as gradual worsening / relief, differences before and after examinations, sleep, and somatic symptoms, forming a symptom timeline to support judgment and conceptualization.
322.when_to_use: In the course-and-change inquiry segment, or when evolution needs sorting out after triggers are confirmed.
322.trigger: When the client recalls when it started, whether it gradually worsened, or differs at specific times (such as around exams).

407.skill_description: Sort out the appearance, worsening, and improvement of symptoms by growth and Learning stages (such as middle school, High school, university), recording duration and key turning points, combining with medical-seeking experiences when necessary, forming a longitudinal illness-course overview.
407.when_to_use: During present illness history collection and longitudinal review, or before diagnosis and conceptualization when cross-stage evolution needs to be clarified.
407.trigger: The client describes cross-stage experiences or clues suggesting symptoms change over time.

367.skill_description: Review key events and psychological reactions in chronological order, linking nodes from setbacks to adaptation difficulties, forming a clear onset-development thread, used to grasp the course and key turning points.
367.when_to_use: After the chief complaint is preliminarily clear, when the starting point and key events need to be located and the illness course organized.
367.trigger: When the client proactively recalls or mentions the impact of several important events on them.

133.skill_name: Map the symptom development sequence and vicious cycles
133.skill_description: Guide describing by the time chain the cycle from Automatic thoughts to emotional reactions, avoidant behaviors, functional decline, and further aggravation, clarifying the illness-course evolution and maintaining mechanisms, providing a basis for subsequent conceptualization and Intervention.
133.when_to_use: When exploring course changes and problem-maintaining factors.
133.trigger: The client reports experiences of emotions and behavior mutually influencing and repeatedly escalating each other.

411.skill_name: Probe precipitating events and build a timeline
411.skill_description: Guide the client to specifically narrate real inducing events and mark their occurrence times, sequentially recording subsequent changes in tension, Anxiety, sleep and appetite, and key nodes, forming a recent evolution timeline.
411.when_to_use: When determining the main problem and conducting the counseling analysis at the first session, or during the trigger-sorting and timeline-building stage.
411.trigger: The client mentions sudden illness in the family, financial pressure, or recent major changes; time markers such as 'at first/subsequently' appear in the narrative.

206.skill_name: Identifying situational triggers and trigger events
206.skill_description: Probe and record trigger situations and negative life events related to the environment, relationships, and Learning tasks, clarifying the event-emotion/behavior chain, locating intervenable trigger points and their social background.
206.when_to_use: When exploring triggers and collecting information for formulating Intervention strategies.
206.trigger: The client mentions distress and stress related to the environment, study arrangements, seasons, or interpersonal changes, with obvious emotional fluctuation after the event.

260.skill_name: Rebuilding the trigger and course timeline
260.skill_description: Review staged events in chronological order up to diagnosis and treatment nodes, record durations and staged changes, forming a clear course axis to grasp evolution patterns and support conceptualization.
260.when_to_use: At the initial assessment stage, conducting illness-course and trigger sorting, or after trigger identification, when systematically depicting the illness-course trajectory.
260.trigger: The client can recall stage-wise events but narrates them in a scattered way, or time markers such as 'starting from the last month', 'after / later' appear.

224.skill_name: Describing the evolution of scope and severity
224.skill_description: Sort out changes in the problem's scope and intensity over time, such as expanding from specific objects to a broader population, from mild discomfort to impulsive behaviors, presenting the symptom development trajectory and functional deterioration.
224.when_to_use: During longitudinal review of the course, used to present changes in symptom range and severity.
224.trigger: The client reports changes such as a widening range of people, behavioral escalation, or increasingly intense emotions.

469.skill_name: Recording coping methods and symptom changes
469.skill_description: Sort out coping styles and their consequences at different stages (such as Avoids socializing, gaming addiction disrupting the daily routine), recording worsening or improvement patterns, connecting the 'coping-outcome-symptom change' chain.
469.when_to_use: After the timeline is established, when needing to identify maintaining factors and coping-outcome relationships.
469.trigger: The client mentions experiences of functioning being further impaired after coping through avoidance, gaming, etc.

149.skill_description: Press questions about the starting time and duration of this problem and compare with the previous state, verify whether it is continuous or intermittent and whether it has worsened, form an outline of the course of illness, and provide a basis for judging severity and intervention timing.
149.when_to_use: In course assessment and severity judgment, or when persistence and change need to be grasped at initial assessment and follow-up.
149.trigger: The client reports vague time words such as 'lasting several days/weeks', 'recently/for a period of time', or has past similar experiences for comparison.

388.skill_name: Clarifying recent precipitating events and starting points
388.skill_description: Clarify and record inducing events such as specific conflicts or relationship changes and their start times, sorting out duration and related situations, forming a timeline of recent symptom triggers and evolution.
388.when_to_use: At the stage of exploring triggers and the illness course, to build timelines and identify trigger factors.
388.trigger: The client mentions a specific conflict event or a locatable start time (such as 'five weeks ago' or 'two months ago').

220.skill_name: Probe the course of precipitating events and interaction details
220.skill_description: Around key conflicts or events triggering the current problem, probe the causes, conversation process, and behavioral responses, identifying direct triggers and possible maintaining-factor clues, refining situational assessment.
220.when_to_use: When the client mentions emotional deterioration after events, needing to clarify trigger factors and interaction details.
220.trigger: When the client mentions specific events such as arguments with father, holiday arrangement conflicts, dormitory disputes.

485.skill_name: Explore cognitive explanations of precipitating events
485.skill_description: Reviews the explanations of the triggering event and changes in beliefs, identifies cognitive-factor clues related to symptom maintenance or worsening such as self-blame and labeling, to supplement trigger and course information.
485.when_to_use: After completing event and timeline sorting, when further exploring the cognitive appraisals related to the triggers.
485.trigger: When the client expresses resentment, a sense of failure, or Self-denial, and other event-related evaluations and inferences.

241.skill_name: Tracking behaviors and changes after precipitation
241.skill_description: Probe specific behaviors taken after triggers (such as deleting, changing seats, avoiding) and their short-term relief and long-term impact, recording changes over time, to identify avoidance and maintaining-mechanism clues.
241.when_to_use: When sorting out the vicious cycle and avoidance maintenance mechanism, connect behavior with symptom changes.
241.trigger: The client narrates avoidance or impulsive behavior and mentions emotions changing accordingly.

319.skill_name: Exploring inducing events and trigger situations
319.skill_description: Sort out the direct inducements and stress sources of the appearance or worsening of problems, list situations such as unfamiliar environments, dense crowds, family conflicts, and isolation, clarify their relationship with the triggering of symptoms, and provide clues for the direction of intervention.
319.when_to_use: At the starting stage of illness-course exploration, when defining trigger situations and preliminarily setting the Intervention direction.
319.trigger: The client mentions that after a recent event, emotion / symptoms clearly worsened, or external stimuli and environmental changes accompanied symptom worsening.

371.skill_name: Build a timeline anchored on major milestones
371.skill_description: Around major nodes such as the postgraduate entrance examination, press questions about the start, peak, key turning points, and duration in days, and sort out in chronological order key nodes such as onset, medical seeking, and relief, forming a clear timeline depicting the changes in the course of illness.
371.when_to_use: After a preliminary understanding of symptoms, when the onset and evolution trajectory need to be clarified, or at the current-history organization stage.
371.trigger: When the client mentions key events like failing the postgraduate entrance exam, breakdown, or abandoning the exam, or provides symptom/medical information at different time points.

174.skill_name: Using the ABC framework to sort out trigger and response chains
174.skill_description: Guide restoring the inducing event A, identifying belief B and emotional/behavioral consequence C, systematically recording trigger factors and response styles, identifying distress-causing cognitions, supporting the exploration and organization of trigger and illness-course changes.
174.when_to_use: When exploring triggers and course, events and psychological reactions need to be collected in a structured way, or when the event-reaction relationship is vague.
174.trigger: When emotions drop sharply due to others' words or situations, with belief statements like 'everyone looks down on me', or clues are scattered and hard to link together.

408.skill_name: Systematically assessing learning and interpersonal functioning
408.skill_description: Around Learning efficiency and attitude, exam and classroom performance, and the quality of interactions with classmates/friends/roommates/teachers, conflicts, and feelings of Loneliness, recording frequency and impact, comparing stage changes, identifying support systems and the scope of impairment, avoiding missed problems.
408.when_to_use: After chief complaint and symptom assessment, entering the social functioning assessment stage, especially for student clients or when Learning and interpersonal sections need verification.
408.trigger: When clues appear like decreased Learning efficiency, affected daily routine, reduced social contact, dormitory conflicts, or Relationship tension.

386.skill_name: Assessing social participation and avoidance limitations
386.skill_description: Around classmate/friend interaction and communication frequency, avoided situations and topics, classroom and group activity participation, recording Reduced socializing, going it alone, unwillingness to come to school, and other manifestations and their impact, determining the degree of interpersonal and campus adaptation limitation.
386.when_to_use: When assessing the scope of social functional impairment and Intervention priorities, covering education and interpersonal domains.
386.trigger: When clues appear like the client being unwilling to communicate, reduced communication, avoiding school, or affected classroom participation.

279.skill_name: Assess peer conflicts and experiences of exclusion
279.skill_description: Record in specific detail the frequency of being talked about behind one's back, teased, told tales on, told to do homework, pranked and humiliated, and assess the impact and scope of isolation and people-pleasing interaction on interpersonal functioning.
279.when_to_use: When social functioning assessment focuses on the campus peer-relationship section or identifying interpersonal risks and resources.
279.trigger: When the client mentions classmate rejection, being mocked/bullied, Relationship tension, or conflict events.

246.skill_name: Mapping the interpersonal network and social support
246.skill_description: Systematically inventory the number of friends and closeness, the relationship quality and communication frequency with roommates/classmates/teachers/parents, identifying support gaps and conflict foci like 'very Loneliness, rarely interacting, poor relationships', defining the scope of social limitation in different domains.
246.when_to_use: At the social functioning and environment assessment stage, when the support network and interaction quality need clarifying.
246.trigger: When the client describes lacking friends, avoiding communication with family, or having interaction difficulties in different relationships/occasions.

401.skill_name: Assess dormitory and classmate interactions and adjustment
401.skill_description: Understand how they get along with classmates/roommates, communication frequency and comfort, recording phenomena like avoidance, tension, and discomfort, and their impact on Learning life, judging whether interpersonal functioning is impaired or stable.
401.when_to_use: At the social functioning assessment stage, focusing on interpersonal interaction and campus adaptation.
401.trigger: Clues about getting along smoothly with classmates/roommates or showing avoidance, tension, staying in the dormitory for long periods, etc.

389.skill_name: Verifying others' feedback and interpersonal perceptions
389.skill_description: Record classmates'/head teacher's feedback to verify social functioning and emotional state, and explore the client's interpersonal views and interaction characteristics (such as being influenced by evaluations, views on relationship length), identifying interpersonal cognitive biases and risks.
389.when_to_use: When functional impairment needs verification or self-report needs supplementation, and when assessing Interpersonal relationships and role functioning.
389.trigger: Obtaining a feedback channel from classmates or the class teacher, or the client talks about classmates' evaluations, romantic experiences, and views on relationships.

346.skill_name: Assessing social support and communication frequency
346.skill_description: Ask about communication frequency with those around them, friends to confide in, and family response styles (Silence, support, or denial), recording 'little communication, lacking support system', etc., judging support availability and gaps, providing a basis for resource mobilization.
346.when_to_use: Social support system and family functioning assessment stage.
346.trigger: When the client shows little communication, no one to talk to, family not yet handling events, or insufficient support.

253.skill_description: Record stable interpersonal patterns such as introverted personality, not good at socializing, sensitive inferiority, people-pleasing tendencies, and lacking true friends, assessing the current state of social functioning and potential interpersonal risks.
253.when_to_use: When comprehensively assessing interpersonal and social adaptation and understanding how interaction style affects relationships.
253.trigger: Clues that the client self-reports social difficulties, low self-esteem, or reliance on people-pleasing to maintain relationships.

171.skill_description: Through session inquiry into changes in study, interpersonal, and activity areas, record reduced socializing and going out, decreased interest, disordered routines, and avoided situations, judge the degree of impairment and the main situations, and provide a basis for intervention priorities.
171.when_to_use: After initial assessment or symptom description is completed, conducting a functional check, or before formulating a behavioral activation and support plan.
171.trigger: The client mentions learning difficulties, reduced activities and interaction, school aversion, or changes in mood and routine.

368.skill_name: Assessing academic adaptation and classroom functioning
368.skill_description: Ask about the adaptation after entering school, attention in class, and the specific manifestations of routines being affected, combined with grades and classroom experiences, define the scope and degree of functional impairment in educational situations and the impact on interpersonal relations.
368.when_to_use: At the overall social-function assessment and problem-scope definition stage, when education/learning roles are involved.
368.trigger: When clues appear like unfocused attention, skipping classes, avoiding class after being humiliated by teachers, grade pressure, and worrying about evaluations.

216.skill_name: Assess the availability and effectiveness of social support
216.skill_description: Record reactions and help received after confiding in roommates, classmates, friends, or family, comparing past and current differences in support use, confirming support withdrawal, communication styles, and available resources.
216.when_to_use: When understanding the Social support system and resource gaps, before formulating a supportive plan or Intervention.
216.trigger: When the client mentions seeking help but not yet receiving it, reducing contact with old classmates, or refusing family/Social support.

179.skill_name: Assessing study and work role functioning
179.skill_description: Around study and work functioning, concretize efficiency, attention, task completion, and attendance, attending also to internships and class work, record 'can study/work normally but efficiency has declined' etc., distinguish severity levels and clarify impaired areas.
179.when_to_use: After chief complaint and symptom collection, turning to Learning/Work functioning assessment or before setting Intervention goals.
179.trigger: The client reports decreased study/work engagement, task omissions, increased criticism, or reduced efficiency.

166.skill_name: Assessing peer relationships and dormitory conflicts
166.skill_description: Ask about the quality of relationships with classmates/roommates, the frequency of quarrels and conflicts, and dispute triggers such as schedules and noise, record subjective feelings and impact, and assess interpersonal functional impairment and adaptation to the educational environment.
